We use the notation as in \cite[Definition~2.4]{HL23a}. Let $X$ be a normal quasi-projective variety. A $\bm{b}$-divisor ${\bf{M}}$ on $X$ is a (possibly infinite) $\mathbb R$-linear combination of divisorial valuations $\nu_P$ over $X$
\[{\bf{M}}=\sum_Pr_P\nu_P\]
such that for any birational map $\phi\colon X\dashrightarrow Y$, 
\[\{P\mid \operatorname{center}_{Y}P\text{ is a divisor}, r_P\neq 0\}\]
is a finite set. By definition, ${\bf{M}}$ is also a $\bm{b}$-divisor on $Y$. We say that ${\bf{M}}$ is a $\mathbb Q$-$\bm{b}$-divisor if $r_P\in\mathbb Q$ for any prime divisor $P$ over $X$. For any birational map $\phi\colon X\dashrightarrow Y$, we denote by
\[{\bf{M}}_{Y}:=\sum_{P\mid \operatorname{center}_{Y}P\text{ is a divisor}}r_P\left(\operatorname{center}_{Y}P\right).\]
We say that ${\bf{M}}$ \emph{descends to} $X$ if ${\bf{M}}_{X}$ is $\mathbb R$-Cartier, and for any projective birational morphism $h\colon X'\rightarrow X$, we have ${\bf{M}}_{X'}=h^*{\bf{M}}_X$. For any $\mathbb R$-Cartier $\mathbb R$-divisor $D$ on $X$, we denote by $\overline{D}$ the $\bm{b}$-divisor ${\bf{M}}$ such that ${\bf{M}}$ descends to $X$ and ${\bf{M}}_X=D$. We denote by $\bm{0}:=\overline{0}$. We say that ${\bf{M}}$ is \emph{$\bm{b}$-Cartier} if there exists a birational map $\phi\colon X\dashrightarrow Y$ such that ${\bf{M}}$ descends to $Y$ and ${\bf{M}}_Y$ is Cartier. For any projective morphism $\pi: X\rightarrow U$, we say that ${\bf{M}}$ is \emph{nef$/U$} (resp. ${\bf{M}}\equiv_{U}\bm{0}$) if there exists a birational map$/U$ $\phi\colon X\dashrightarrow Y$ such that ${\bf{M}}$ descends to $Y$ and ${\bf{M}}_Y$ is nef$/U$ (resp. ${\bf{M}}_Y\equiv_{U}0$), and if $U$ is a closed point, then we say that ${\bf{M}}$ is \emph{nef} (resp. ${\bf{M}}\equiv\bm{0}$). We denote by $\mathrm{bNef}(X/U)$ the set of nef$/U$ $\bm{b}$-divisors on $X$. We denote by $\mathrm{bNef}(X):=\mathrm{bNef}(X/\{pt\})$. We refer the reader to \cite[Remark~4.2(2), Definition~4.7]{BZ16} for restriction of $\bm{b}$-divisors to the general fiber of a contraction or to the normalization of a prime divisor, which we will often use in this paper.

\label{defn: foliation}
Let $X$ be a normal quasi-projective variety. 
A \emph{foliation} $\mathcal{F}$ on $X$ is a coherent sheaf $T_{\mathcal{F}}\subset T_X$ such that $T_{\mathcal{F}}$ is saturated in $T_X$ and $T_{\mathcal{F}}$ is closed under the Lie bracket. 
The \emph{rank} of $\mathcal{F}$ is the rank of $T_{\mathcal{F}}$ as a sheaf and is denoted by $\operatorname{rank}\mathcal{F}$. 
The \emph{canonical divisor} of $\mathcal{F}$ is a divisor $K_{\mathcal{F}}$ such that $\mathcal{O}_X(-K_{\mathcal{F}})\cong\det(T_{\mathcal{F}})$. 
We say that $\mathcal{F}$ is \emph{$\mathbb Q$-Gorenstein} if $K_{\mathcal{F}}$ is $\mathbb Q$-Cartier.


A subvariety $S\subset X$ is called \emph{$\mathcal{F}$-invariant} if for any open subset $U\subset X$ and any section $\partial\in H^0(U,T_{\mathcal{F}})$, we have $\partial(\mathcal{I}_{S\cap U})\subset \mathcal{I}_{S\cap U}$, where $\mathcal{I}_{S\cap U}$ denotes the ideal sheaf of $S\cap U$ in $U$. 

Given any dominant map 
$h\colon Y\dashrightarrow X$, we denote by $h^{-1}\mathcal{F}$ the \emph{pullback} of $\mathcal{F}$ on $Y$ (cf.~\cite[\S~3.2]{Dru21}). We say that $\mathcal{F}$ is \emph{algebraically integrable} if there exists a dominant map $f\colon X\dashrightarrow Z$ such that $\mathcal{F}=f^{-1}\mathcal{F}_Z$, where $\mathcal{F}_Z$ is the trivial foliation (i.e.\ $T_{\mathcal{F}_Z}=0$), and we say that $\mathcal{F}$ is \emph{induced by} $f$. 

Fix a birational map
$g\colon X\dashrightarrow X'$, and define $g_\ast \mathcal{F}\coloneqq (g^{-1})^{-1}\mathcal{F}$. 
For any prime divisor $P$ over $X$ such that $P':=\operatorname{center}_{X'}P$ is a divisor, we write $\epsilon_{\mathcal{F}}(P):=0$ (resp. $\epsilon_{\mathcal{F}}(P):=1$) if $P'$ is (resp. is not) $g_*\mathcal{F}$-invariant. 
For any $\mathbb R$-divisor $D=\sum_{i=1}^na_iD_i$ on $X$ where each $D_i$ is a prime divisor, we write $D_{\mathcal{F}}^{\operatorname{ninv}}:=\sum_{i=1}^n\epsilon_{\mathcal{F}}(D_i)a_iD_i$ and $D_{\mathcal{F}}^{\operatorname{inv}}:=D-D_{\mathcal{F}}^{\operatorname{ninv}}$. 
If $\mathcal{F}$ is clear in the context then we may write
$D^{\operatorname{ninv}}:=D_{\mathcal{F}}^{\operatorname{ninv}}$ and $D^{\operatorname{inv}}:=D_{\mathcal{F}}^{\operatorname{inv}}$.

A \emph{foliated pair} is a pair $(X,\mathcal{F})$ consisting of a normal variety $X$ and a foliation $\mathcal{F}$ on $X$.

\label{defn: afs}
An \emph{adjoint foliated structure}, denoted by
\[
{\mathfrak{A}}/U=(X,\mathcal{F},B,{\bf{M}},t)/U,
\]
consists of a normal quasi-projective variety $X$ equipped with a projective morphism $X\to U$, a foliation $\mathcal{F}$ on $X$, an $\mathbb{R}$-divisor $B\geq 0$ on $X$, a nef$/U$ $\bm{b}$-divisor ${\bf{M}}$ on $X$, and a real number $t\in [0,1]$, such that the $\mathbb{R}$-divisor
\[
K_{{\mathfrak{A}}}:=tK_{\mathcal{F}}+(1-t)K_X+B+{\bf{M}}_X
\]
is $\mathbb{R}$-Cartier. The \emph{dimension} $\dim{\mathfrak{A}}$ of ${\mathfrak{A}}$ is defined to be $\dim X$.

If we allow $B$ to have negative coefficients, then we add the prefix ``sub-''. If $B$ is a $\mathbb{Q}$-divisor, ${\bf{M}}$ is a $\mathbb{Q}$-$\bm{b}$-divisor, and $t\in\mathbb Q$, then we add the prefix ``$\mathbb{Q}$-''. If we do not require $K_{{\mathfrak{A}}}$ to be $\mathbb{R}$-Cartier, then we add the prefix ``quasi-''.

Let ${\mathfrak{A}}/U=(X,\mathcal{F},B,{\bf{M}},t)/U$ be a quasi-sub-adjoint foliated structure.

We call $X,\mathcal{F},B,{\bf{M}},t$ the \emph{ambient variety}, \emph{foliation part}, \emph{boundary part}, \emph{nef part} (or \emph{moduli part}), and \emph{parameter} of ${\mathfrak{A}}$, respectively. $K_{{\mathfrak{A}}}$ is called the \emph{canonical $\mathbb R$-divisor} of ${\mathfrak{A}}$. The $\mathbb R$-divisor $B+{\bf{M}}_X$ is called the \emph{generalized boundary} of ${\mathfrak{A}}$. 
We adopt the following abbreviations:
\begin{align*}
  {\mathfrak{A}}=(X,\mathcal{F},B,{\bf{M}}) &\quad\text{if } t=1,\ \text{and then }{\mathfrak{A}}/U\text{ is called a \emph{generalized foliated quadruple}},\\
  {\mathfrak{A}}=(X,B,{\bf{M}}) &\quad\text{if } \mathcal{F}=T_X\ \text{or } t=0,\ \text{and then }{\mathfrak{A}}/U\text{ is called a \emph{generalized pair}},\\
  {\mathfrak{A}}=(X,\mathcal{F},B) &\quad\text{if } {\bf{M}}=\bm{0}\ \text{and } t=1,\ \text{and then }{\mathfrak{A}}/U\text{ is called a \emph{foliated triple}},\\
  {\mathfrak{A}}=(X,B) &\quad\text{if }{\mathfrak{A}}\text{ is a generalized pair and }{\bf{M}}=\bm{0},\ \text{and then }{\mathfrak{A}}/U\text{ is called a \emph{pair}}.
\end{align*}


If $B=0$, or if ${\bf{M}}=\bm{0}$, or if $U$ is not important, then we may drop $B,{\bf{M}},U$ respectively. If $U=\{pt\}$ then we also drop $U$ and say that ${\mathfrak{A}}$ is \emph{projective}. 

For any $\mathbb{R}$-divisor $D$ on $X$ and nef$/U$ $\bm{b}$-divisor ${\bf{N}}$ on $X$, we denote by $({\mathfrak{A}},D,{\bf{N}}):=(X,\mathcal{F},B+D,{\bf{M}}+{\bf{N}},t)$. If $D=0$ or ${\bf{N}}=\bm{0}$ then we may drop $D,{\bf{N}}$ respectively. 

We say that ${\mathfrak{A}}$ is \emph{algebraically integrable} if $\mathcal{F}$ is, and that ${\mathfrak{A}}$ is \emph{$\mathbb Q$-factorial} if $X$ is.

Let ${\mathfrak{A}}_i/U=(X,\mathcal{F},B_i,{\bf{M}}_i,t_i)/U$, $i=1, \dots, k$ be quasi-sub-adjoint foliated structures. 
For all $1 \leq i \leq k$, let $a_i\in\mathbb R_{\geq 0}$ be real numbers such that 
$\sum_{i=1}^k a_it_i\leq 1$. 
We write
\begin{align*}
\sum_{i=1}^k a_i{\mathfrak{A}}_i:=\left(X,\mathcal{F},\sum_{i=1}^k a_iB_i,\sum_{i=1}^k a_i{\bf{M}}_i,\sum_{i=1}^k a_it_i\right).
\end{align*}
Let us note that if $\sum_{i=1}^k a_i=1$, then $K_{\sum_{i=1}^k a_i{\mathfrak{A}}_i}=\sum_{i=1}^k a_iK_{{\mathfrak{A}}_i}$.

We shall say that the adjoint foliated structure A/U defined above is the adjoint foliated structure associated to B/U, and we denote this relation by \[ A=logB. \] The dimension dimB of B is defined to be dim X. We denote this inverse correspondence by B=exp(A).

We refer to X,F,B,bfM,t as the ambient variety, foliation part, boundary part, nef part (or moduli part), and parameter of B, respectively. We write K_Bcoloneqq K_A and call it the canonical mathbb R-divisor of B. If B=0, or bfM=bm0, or the base U is clear from the context, then we may drop B, bfM, or U, respectively. For any mathbb R-divisor D on X and nef/U bmb-divisor bfN on X, we set \[ (B,D,bfN)coloneqq (X,F,B+D,bfM+bfN)(t). \] If D=0 or bfN=bm0, then we may drop D or bfN, respectively. We say that B is algebraically integrable (resp. mathbb Q-factorial) if logB is algebraically integrable (resp. mathbb Q-factorial), i.e.\ if F is (resp. X is). Let ${\mathfrak{B}}/U=(X,\mathcal{F},B,{\bf{M}})(t)$ be a quasi-sub-normalized foliated structure, and set ${\mathfrak{A}}:=\log{\mathfrak{B}}$.
We refer to $X,\mathcal{F},B,{\bf{M}},t$ as the \emph{ambient variety}, \emph{foliation part}, \emph{boundary part}, \emph{nef part} (or \emph{moduli part}), and \emph{parameter} of ${\mathfrak{B}}$, respectively.
We write $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}}\coloneqq K_{{\mathfrak{A}}}$ and call it the \emph{canonical $\mathbb R$-divisor} of ${\mathfrak{B}}$.

If $B=0$, or ${\bf{M}}=\bm{0}$, or the base $U$ is clear from the context, then we may drop $B$, ${\bf{M}}$, or $U$, respectively.
If $U=\{pt\}$, then we also drop $U$ and say that ${\mathfrak{B}}$ is \emph{projective}.

We say that ${\mathfrak{B}}/U$ is \emph{of general type} if $(\log{\mathfrak{B}})/U$ is of general type.
For any $\mathbb R$-divisor $D$ on $X$ and nef$/U$ $\bm{b}$-divisor ${\bf{N}}$ on $X$, we set
\[
({\mathfrak{B}},D,{\bf{N}})\coloneqq (X,\mathcal{F},B+D,{\bf{M}}+{\bf{N}})(t).
\]
If $D=0$ or ${\bf{N}}=\bm{0}$, then we may drop $D$ or ${\bf{N}}$, respectively.

We say that ${\mathfrak{B}}$ is \emph{algebraically integrable} (resp. \emph{$\mathbb Q$-factorial}) if $\log{\mathfrak{B}}$ is algebraically integrable (resp. $\mathbb Q$-factorial), i.e.\ if $\mathcal{F}$ is (resp. $X$ is).

A \emph{foliated log resolution} of ${\mathfrak{B}}$ is a foliated log resolution of $(X,\mathcal{F},\operatorname{Supp} B,{\bf{M}})$ (cf.~\cite[Definition~6.2.3]{CHLX23}).

For any set $\Gamma\subset [0,+\infty)$, we write ${\mathfrak{B}}/U\in\Gamma$ if $B,t\in\Gamma$ and ${\bf{M}}=\sum\mu_j{\bf{M}}_j$, where each $\mu_j\in\Gamma$ and each ${\bf{M}}_j$ is nef$/U$ $\bm{b}$-Cartier.

We say that B/U is mathbb R-complementary if B/U has an mathbb R-complement. Let B be a projective normalized foliated structure. We denote by alpha(B):=alpha(logB). Let ${\mathfrak{B}}/U$ be an lc normalized foliated structure. An \emph{$\mathbb R$-complement} of ${\mathfrak{B}}/U$ is an lc normalized foliated structure $({\mathfrak{B}},D)/U$ such that $D\geq 0$ and $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}}+D\sim_{\mathbb R,U}0$. We say that ${\mathfrak{B}}/U$ is \emph{$\mathbb R$-complementary} if ${\mathfrak{B}}/U$ has an $\mathbb R$-complement. 

Let ${\mathfrak{B}}$ be a projective normalized foliated structure. We denote by $\alpha({\mathfrak{B}}):=\alpha(\log{\mathfrak{B}})$. We say that ${\mathfrak{B}}$ is \emph{Fano} if $-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}}$ is ample. We say that ${\mathfrak{B}}$ is \emph{exceptional} if $|-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}}|_{\mathbb R}\neq\emptyset$ and $({\mathfrak{B}},D)$ is klt for any $0\leq D\sim_{\mathbb R}-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}}$.

\label{lem: geometric average of nfs}
Let ${\mathfrak{B}}/U=(X,\mathcal{F},B,{\bf{M}})(t)/U$ and ${\mathfrak{B}}'/U=(X,\mathcal{F},B',{\bf{M}}')(t')/U$ be two quasi-sub-normalized foliated structures and let $s\in [0,1]$ be a real number. Let ${\mathfrak{A}}=\log{\mathfrak{B}}$ and ${\mathfrak{A}}'=\log{\mathfrak{B}}'$. Set $t_s := st+(1-s)t'$ and denote
\[(X,\mathcal{F},\Gamma_s,{\bf{N}}_s,t_s):= s{\mathfrak{A}}+(1-s){\mathfrak{A}}'\] and \[(X,\mathcal{F},B_s,{\bf{M}}_s)(t_s):={\mathfrak{B}}^s+{\mathfrak{B}}'^{1-s}\]
(note that it follows from the definition that the parameter in each of these structures is equal to $t_s$).
Similarly, let us denote \[(X,\mathcal{F},\Delta_s,{\bf{M}}_s,t_s):=\log({\mathfrak{B}}^s+{\mathfrak{B}}'^{1-s})\]
for any $s\in [0,1]$. Then the following hold. 
\begin{enumerate}
    \item For any $s\in [0,1]$, we have 
\[{\bf{N}}_s={\bf{M}}_s=s{\bf{M}}+(1-s){\bf{M}}'.\]
\item For any $s\in [0,1]$, we have 
\[\Delta_s-\Gamma_s=s(1-s)(t-t')(B^{\operatorname{inv}}-B'^{\operatorname{inv}}).\]
In particular,
$\Gamma_s^{\operatorname{ninv}}=\Delta_s^{\operatorname{ninv}}=(sB+(1-s)B')^{\operatorname{ninv}}$.
\item Assume that ${\mathfrak{B}}/U\geq{\mathfrak{B}}'/U$ or ${\mathfrak{B}}'/U\geq{\mathfrak{B}}/U$. Then $\Delta_s\geq\Gamma_s$ for any $s\in [0,1]$. Moreover, $\Delta_s=\Gamma_s$ if and only if $s=0$ or $1$, or $t=t'$, or $B^{\operatorname{inv}}=B'^{\operatorname{inv}}$.
\item Assume that $t\neq1$ (resp. $t'\neq1$). Then for any $s\in (0,1]$ (resp. $s \in [0,1)$),  $\exp(s{\mathfrak{A}}+(1-s){\mathfrak{A}}')$ is well defined. Moreover:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item If ${\mathfrak{B}}/U\geq{\mathfrak{B}}'/U$ or ${\mathfrak{B}}'/U\geq{\mathfrak{B}}/U$, then 
\[({\mathfrak{B}}^s+{\mathfrak{B}}'^{1-s})/U\geq\exp(s{\mathfrak{A}}+(1-s){\mathfrak{A}}')/U,\]
and equality holds when $s=0$ or $1$, or $t=t'$, or $B^{\operatorname{inv}}=B'^{\operatorname{inv}}$. 
\item If ${\mathfrak{B}}/U\geq{\mathfrak{B}}'/U$, then for any $1>s\geq r>0$, 
\[\exp\left(s{\mathfrak{A}}+(1-s){\mathfrak{A}}'\right)/U\geq\exp\left(r{\mathfrak{A}}+(1-r){\mathfrak{A}}'\right)/U.\]
Moreover, ${\mathfrak{B}}/U\geq \exp(s{\mathfrak{A}}+(1-s){\mathfrak{A}}')/U\geq{\mathfrak{B}}'/U$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}

By definition,
\begin{align*}
{\mathfrak{A}} = (X, \mathcal F, B^{\operatorname{ninv}} +(1-t)B^{\operatorname{inv}}, {\bf{M}}, t)
\ \text{and} \
{\mathfrak{A}}' = (X, \mathcal F, B'^{\operatorname{ninv}}+(1-t')B'^{\operatorname{inv}}, {\bf{M}}', t').
\end{align*}
Thus,
\begin{align*}
&s{\mathfrak{A}}+(1-s){\mathfrak{A}}' =  \\ &(X,\mathcal{F},s(B^{\operatorname{ninv}}+(1-t)B^{\operatorname{inv}})+(1-s)(B'^{\operatorname{ninv}}+(1-t')B'^{\operatorname{inv}}),s{\bf{M}}+(1-s){\bf{M}}',t_s)= \\
&(X, \mathcal F, (sB+(1-s)B')^{\operatorname{ninv}}+(s(1-t)B+(1-s)(1-t')B')^{\operatorname{inv}}, s{\bf{M}}+(1-s){\bf{M}}', t_s).
\end{align*}
On the other hand, we have
\begin{align*}
{\mathfrak{B}}^s+{\mathfrak{B}}'^{1-s} = (X, \mathcal F, sB+(1-s)B', s{\bf{M}}+(1-s){\bf{M}}', t_s).    
\end{align*}
Hence, 
\begin{align*}
&{\mathfrak{A}}_s:= \log ({\mathfrak{B}}^s+{\mathfrak{B}}'^{1-s}) = \\
&(X, \mathcal F, (sB+(1-s)B')^{\operatorname{ninv}}+(1-t_s)(sB+(1-s)B')^{\operatorname{inv}}, s{\bf{M}}+(1-s){\bf{M}}', t_s).
\end{align*}
From this we can conclude that:
\begin{itemize}
    \item 
(1) follows immediately from the above expressions.
    \item 
For (2), the above expressions imply that 
\[\Gamma_s = (sB+(1-s)B')^{\operatorname{ninv}}+(s(1-t)B+(1-s)(1-t')B')^{\operatorname{inv}}\]
and 
\[\Delta_s = (sB+(1-s)B')^{\operatorname{ninv}}+(1-t_s)(sB+(1-s)B')^{\operatorname{inv}},\]
from which in turn the claimed equality follows at once.





    \item 
Since ${\mathfrak{B}}/U\geq{\mathfrak{B}}'/U$ or ${\mathfrak{B}}'/U\geq{\mathfrak{B}}/U$, $(t-t')(B^{\operatorname{inv}}-B'^{\operatorname{inv}})\geq 0$. Hence, we can conclude that (3) follows from (2). 
    \item 
Finally, (4.a) follows from (3) since $t_s<1$ implies that $\exp(s{\mathfrak{A}}+(1-s){\mathfrak{A}}')$ is well-defined. 
To prove (4.b), let us note that when ${\mathfrak{B}}/U\geq{\mathfrak{B}}'/U$, then $B\geq B'$; hence,

$\Gamma_s^{\operatorname{ninv}}-\Gamma_r^{\operatorname{ninv}}=(s-r)(B^{\operatorname{ninv}}-B^{\operatorname{inv}})\geq 0$,

and
\begin{align*}
    \frac{1}{1-t_s}\Gamma_s^{\operatorname{inv}}-\frac{1}{1-t_r}\Gamma_r^{\operatorname{inv}}=\frac{(s-r)(1-t')(1-t)}{(1-t_s)(1-t_r)}(B^{\operatorname{inv}}-B'^{\operatorname{inv}})\geq 0,
\end{align*}
which implies that 
$\exp(s{\mathfrak{A}}+(1-s){\mathfrak{A}}')/U\geq\exp(r{\mathfrak{A}}+(1-r){\mathfrak{A}}')/U$.
\end{itemize}

Let 
${\mathfrak{B}}/U$ and ${\mathfrak{B}}'/U$ 
be normalized foliated structures with ambient variety $X$. By the above definition, if 
${\mathfrak{B}}/U\geq{\mathfrak{B}}'/U$ or ${\mathfrak{B}}'/U\geq{\mathfrak{B}}/U$, 
then
\begin{align*}
({\mathfrak{B}}^s+{\mathfrak{B}}'^{1-s})/U\geq ({\mathfrak{B}}^s\cdot{\mathfrak{B}}'^{1-s})/U,
\end{align*}
and equality holds if and only if either $s=0, 1$, or $t=t'$, or $B^{\operatorname{inv}}=B'^{\operatorname{inv}}$.
If ${\mathfrak{B}}/U\geq{\mathfrak{B}}'/U$, then
  \[{\mathfrak{B}}/U\geq({\mathfrak{B}}^s+{\mathfrak{B}}'^{1-s})/U\geq{\mathfrak{B}}^s\cdot{\mathfrak{B}}'^{1-s}/U\geq{\mathfrak{B}}'/U.\]
Moreover, the function $s\mapsto {\mathfrak{B}}^s\cdot{\mathfrak{B}}'^{1-s}/U$ is increasing with respect to the ordering $\geq$.

When $s \in (0, 1)$ it is usually unclear whether ${\mathfrak{B}}^s+{\mathfrak{B}}'^{1-s}$ is in turn a normalized foliated structure: indeed, it may not be the case in general that $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}^s+{\mathfrak{B}}'^{1-s}}$ is $\mathbb R$-Cartier.

\label{defn: bounded pairs}
We say that a set 
$\mathcal{P}$ 
of projective varieties is 
\emph{birationally bounded} 
if there exists a projective morphism 
$f\colon Z\rightarrow T$, 
where 
$T$ 
is of finite type, such that for every 
$X\in\mathcal{P}$, 
there exists a closed point 
$t\in T$
such that
$Z_t:=f^{-1}(t)$
is irreducible, together with
a birational map 
$\phi_t \colon Z_t\dashrightarrow X$.

We say that a set 
$\mathcal{P}$ 
of pairs is \emph{log birationally bounded} 
(resp. \emph{bounded}) 
if there is a pair 
$(Z,C)$ 
such that 
$C$ 
is reduced, 
and a projective morphism 
$f \colon Z\rightarrow T$ 
where 
$T$ 
is of finite type, such that for any pair
$(X,B)\in\mathcal{P}$, 
there exists a closed point 
$t\in T$
such that 
$Z_t:=f^{-1}(t)$
is irreducible, together with
a birational map (resp. isomorphism) 
$\phi_t \colon Z_t\dashrightarrow X$ 
such that 
\begin{align*}
\operatorname{Supp} C_t\neq Z_t
\quad 
\text{and}
\quad  
(\phi^{-1}_t)_\ast \operatorname{Supp} B
\cup
\operatorname{Exc}(\phi_t)
\subset
\operatorname{Supp} C_t\ \left(\text{resp. }\phi_t(C_t)=B\right),
\end{align*}
where $C_t:=f^{-1}(t)\cap C$.

\label{defn: bounded foliated pairs}
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a set of projective foliated pairs $(X,\mathcal{F})$. We say that $\mathcal{P}$ is \emph{bounded} if there exist finitely many flat projective morphisms 
$f_i\colon X_i\to Z_i$, 
$i=1,\dots,N$ 
of normal varieties with normal fibers and foliations $\mathcal G_i$ of rank $r_i$ on $X_i$ satisfying the following properties:
 \begin{enumerate}
    \item For any closed point $z\in Z_i$
    with $X_{i,z}:=f_i^{-1}(z)$, we have $T_{X_i/Z_i}|_{X_{i,z}}\simeq T_{X_{i,z}}$.
    \item $T_{\mathcal G_i}\subset T_{X_i/Z_i}$, and for any closed point 
    $z\in Z_i$, we have that $T_{\mathcal G_i}|_{X_{i,z}}\subset T_{X_{i,z}}$ defines a foliation ${\mathcal{F}_{i,z}}$ of rank $r_i$ on $X_{i,z}$.
    \item For any $(X,\mathcal F)\in \mathcal P$, there exist $i\in\{1,\dots,N\}$, a closed point $z\in Z_i$, and an isomorphism $\phi_z\colon X\to X_{i,z}$, such that $(\phi_z)_\ast\mathcal F\simeq \mathcal F_{i,z}$.
    \end{enumerate}
    In particular, $\{X\mid X\in\mathcal{P}\}$ is bounded.

 Let $\Gamma\subset [0,+\infty)$ be a DCC set and $\Gamma_0\subset [0,+\infty)$ a discrete set. Then there exists a finite set $\Gamma_0'$ depending only on $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma_0$ satisfying the following. Assume that:
\begin{enumerate}
\item ${\mathfrak{B}}/U:=(X,\mathcal{F},B,{\bf{M}})(t)/U$ is a $\mathbb Q$-factorial lc algebraically integrable normalized foliated structure,
\item $B\in\Gamma$, $t\in\Gamma\backslash\{1\}$, and ${\bf{M}}=\sum \mu_j{\bf{M}}_j$, where $\mu_j\in\Gamma$ and ${\bf{M}}_j$ is nef$/U$ $\bm{b}$-Cartier.
\item $D\in\Gamma$ is an $\mathbb{R}$-divisor on $X$ and ${\bf{N}}=\sum\nu_k{\bf{N}}_k$, where each ${\bf{N}}_k$ is nef$/U$ $\bm{b}$-Cartier and each $\nu_k\in\Gamma$.
\item $S$ is a normal prime divisor on $X$ such that $S$ is an lc place of 
$${\mathfrak{B}}':=({\mathfrak{B}},D,{\bf{N}}),$$
$S$ is not a component of $D$, and $(X,S)$ is plt.
\item ${\mathfrak{B}}_S/U=\left(S,\mathcal{F}_S,\Delta_S,{\bf{P}}^S\right)(t)/U$ is the lc algebraically integrable normalized foliated structure induced by adjunction
$$K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_S}:=K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'}|_S,$$
where ${\bf{P}}^S=\sum \mu_j{\bf{M}}_j^S+\sum\nu_k{\bf{N}}_k^S$, ${\bf{M}}_j^S :={\bf{M}}_j|_S$, and ${\bf{N}}_k^S :={\bf{N}}_k|_S$ for any $j,k$.
\item $F$ is a general fiber of $g: S\rightarrow Z$ where $S\xrightarrow{g} Z\xrightarrow{\tau} U$ is the Stein factorization of the induced morphism $S\rightarrow Z$.
\item $\Delta_S|_F\in\Gamma_0$.
\item For each $k$, either $\nu_k\in\Gamma_0$, or ${\bf{N}}_{k}^S\big|_F\equiv\bm{0}$.
\item For any irreducible component $L$ of $D$, $L|_S\neq0$ over the generic point of $Z$.
\end{enumerate}
Then 
$$D\in\Gamma_0'\quad \text{and} \quad \{\nu_k\mid ({\bf{N}}_{k,X}|_S)|_F\not\equiv 0\}\subset\Gamma_0'.$$

Since $(X,S)$ is plt, $X$ is klt near $\eta_D$ and $S$ is normal, so we may assume that $X$ is $\mathbb Q$-factorial by shrinking $X$ to a neighborhood of $\eta_D$.

(1) follows from \cite[16.6 Proposition]{Kol+92}. Moreover, by  \cite[16.6 Proposition]{Kol+92}, $X$ has a cyclic quotient singularity at $\eta_D$ and $K_X+S$ generates the local class group at $\eta_D$. Let $q\colon Y\rightarrow X$ be the index one cover associated to $K_X+S$ and let $T:=q^{-1}(S)$. By \cite[16.6 Proposition]{Kol+92}, $T$ is irreducible and normal, and the ramification index of $q|_T: T\rightarrow S$ at $E:=q^{-1}(D)$ is exactly $r$. 

Set $\mathcal{F}_Y:=q^{-1}\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{F}_T:=\mathcal{F}_Y|_T$, then $K_{\mathcal{F}_Y}$ and $T$ are both Cartier. By \cite[Proposition-Definition~3.7]{CS25a}, we may write
$$(K_{\mathcal{F}_T}+\epsilon_{\mathcal{F}_Y}(T)T)|_T=K_{\mathcal{F}_T}+aE$$
where $a\geq 0$ is an integer.

We show that $a$ satisfies our requirements. Write
$$(K_{\mathcal{F}}+\epsilon_{\mathcal{F}}(S)S)|_S=K_{\mathcal{F}_S}+cD$$
near the generic point of $D$. Since $r$ is the ramification index of $q|_T$ at $E$, by the Riemann-Hurwitz formula (cf.~\cite[Lemma~3.4]{Dru21} and \cite[Proposition~2.2]{CS25b}), we have
$$a=rc-\epsilon_{\mathcal{F}_S}(D)(r-1)$$
or, equivalently,
$$c=\frac{a+\epsilon_{\mathcal{F}_S}(D)(r-1)}{r}.$$
This implies (2).

We now prove (3) and (4). By \cite[Corollary~5.14]{Dru21}, $\eta_D \in \mathrm{Sing}~\mathcal{F}$ if and only if $\eta_E \in \mathrm{Sing}~\mathcal{F}_Y$, where $\eta_E$ is the generic point of $E$. Thus possibly replacing $(X,S),D$ and $\mathcal{F}$ by $(Y,T),E$ and $\mathcal{F}_Y$, we may assume that $(X,S)$ is log smooth. 

We prove (3). It suffices to show that $a \neq 0$ if and only if $\eta_D \in \mathrm{Sing}(\mathcal{F})$. By \cite[Proposition~3.14(1)]{CS25a} we see that if $\eta_D\in\mathrm{Sing}(\mathcal{F})$, then $a \neq 0$. Since $D\subset S$, if $a \neq 0$, then the image of $\phi$ is contained in the ideal of $D$ in $X$, i.e.\ $\eta_D \in \mathrm{Sing}(\mathcal F)$.

Assume that $X$ is a normal quasi-projective variety, $\mathcal{F}$ a foliation on $X$, and $\widetilde{S}$ a prime divisor on $X$ with normalization $\nu: S\rightarrow\widetilde S$. Assume that there exists a closed subset $Z\subset X$ such that $X\backslash Z$ is $\mathbb Q$-factorial, and $\dim (\widetilde S\cap Z)\leq\dim\widetilde S-2$. Then there exists a canonically defined function $$\operatorname{Diff}_{S}(\mathcal{F},\cdot,\cdot,\cdot): \operatorname{Weil}_{\mathbb R}(X)_{\widetilde{S}=0}\times\mathrm{bNef}(X/X)\times [0,1]\rightarrow\operatorname{Weil}_{\mathbb R}(S)$$
defined in the following way (cf.~Notation~\ref{nota: special notation} for the definition of $\operatorname{Weil}_{\mathbb R}(X)_{\widetilde{S}=0}$).


For any $B\in\operatorname{Weil}_{\mathbb R}(X)_{\widetilde{S}=0}$, ${\bf{M}}\in\mathrm{bNef}(X/X)$, and $t\in [0,1]$, we define:
\begin{itemize}
    \item $\operatorname{Diff}_S(\mathcal{F},B,{\bf{M}},1):=\operatorname{Diff}(\mathcal{F},B)+({\bf{M}}_X|_S-{\bf{M}}^S_S)$ is the unique $\mathbb R$-divisor such that
    $$(K_{\mathcal{F}}+\epsilon_{\mathcal{F}}(\widetilde S)\widetilde S+B+{\bf{M}}_X)|_S=K_{\mathcal{F}_S}+\operatorname{Diff}_S(\mathcal{F},B,{\bf{M}},1)+{\bf{M}}^S_S$$
    where ${\bf{M}}^S:={\bf{M}}|_S$, and $\mathcal{F}_S$ and $\operatorname{Diff}(\mathcal{F},B)$ are the canonically defined foliation and different as in \cite[Proposition-Definition~3.7]{CS25a}. Note that \cite[Proposition-Definition~3.7]{CS25a} defines $\operatorname{Diff}(\mathcal{F},B)$ only when $B\geq 0$ but $\operatorname{Diff}(\mathcal{F},\cdot)$ linearly extends to a function over $\operatorname{Weil}_{\mathbb R}(X)_{\widetilde{S}=0}$.
    \item $\operatorname{Diff}_S(\mathcal{F},B,{\bf{M}},0)$ is the unique $\mathbb R$-divisor such that
        $$(K_{X}+\widetilde S+B+{\bf{M}}_X)|_S=K_{S}+\operatorname{Diff}_S(\mathcal{F},B,{\bf{M}},0)+{\bf{M}}^S_S$$
        by the usual adjunction formula for generalized pairs.
        \item $\operatorname{Diff}_S(\mathcal{F},B,{\bf{M}},t):=t\operatorname{Diff}_S(\mathcal{F},B,{\bf{M}},1)+(1-t)\operatorname{Diff}_S(\mathcal{F},B,{\bf{M}},0)$.
\end{itemize}
The following properties hold:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item If $B\geq 0$, then $\operatorname{Diff}_S(\mathcal{F},B,{\bf{M}},t)\geq 0$.
    \item $\operatorname{Diff}_S(\mathcal{F},B,{\bf{M}},\cdot)$ is a $\mathbb Q$-affine function.
    \item $\operatorname{Diff}_S(\mathcal{F},B,{\bf{M}},t)=\operatorname{Diff}_S(\mathcal{F},0,0,t)+B|_S+\left({\bf{M}}_X|_S-{\bf{M}}^S_S\right)$.
    \item $\operatorname{Diff}_S(\mathcal{F},\cdot,\cdot,t)$ is a $\mathbb Q$-affine function for any $t\in\mathbb Q$.
    \item We have
    $$\operatorname{Diff}_S(\mathcal{F},B^{\operatorname{ninv}}+(1-t)B^{\operatorname{inv}},{\bf{M}},t)=t\operatorname{Diff}_S(\mathcal{F},B^{\operatorname{ninv}},{\bf{M}},1)+(1-t)\operatorname{Diff}_S\left(\mathcal{F},B,{\bf{M}},0\right).$$

We first assume that $X$ is $\mathbb Q$-factorial.

(1) 
It follows from \cite[Proposition-Definition~3.7]{CS25a} that $\operatorname{Diff}(\mathcal{F},B)\geq 0$ if $B\geq 0$. By Lemma~\ref{lem: bnef adjunction effectivity}, ${\bf{M}}_X|_S-{\bf{M}}^S_S\geq 0$, hence $\operatorname{Diff}_S(\mathcal{F},B,{\bf{M}},1)\geq 0$. By the usual adjunction formula for generalized pairs (cf.~\cite[Definition~4.7]{BZ16}), $\operatorname{Diff}_S(\mathcal{F},B,{\bf{M}},0)\geq 0$, so $\operatorname{Diff}_S(\mathcal{F},B,{\bf{M}},t)\geq 0$.

(2) By definition.

(3) By \cite[Proposition-Definition~3.7]{CS25a}, $\operatorname{Diff}(\mathcal{F},B)=\operatorname{Diff}(\mathcal{F},0)+B|_S$, so $$\operatorname{Diff}_S(\mathcal{F},B,{\bf{M}},1)=\operatorname{Diff}_S(\mathcal{F},0,0,1)+B|_S+\left({\bf{M}}_X|_S-{\bf{M}}^S_S\right).$$ By the usual adjunction formula for generalized pairs, $\operatorname{Diff}_S(\mathcal{F},B,{\bf{M}},0)=\operatorname{Diff}_S(\mathcal{F},0,0,0)+B|_S+\left({\bf{M}}_X|_S-{\bf{M}}^S_S\right)$. This implies (3).

(4)(5) follow from (3).

Now for the general case, let $X^0:=X\backslash Z$, $\widetilde S^0:=X^0\cap\widetilde{S}$, and $S^0:=\nu^{-1}(\widetilde{S})$. By the $\mathbb Q$-factorial case, there exists a canonically defined function
$$\operatorname{Diff}_{S^0}(\mathcal{F}|_{X^0},\cdot,\cdot,\cdot):\operatorname{Weil}_{\mathbb R}(X^0)_{\widetilde{S}^0}\times\mathrm{bNef}(X^0/X^0)\times [0,1]\rightarrow\operatorname{Weil}_{\mathbb R}(S^0)$$
Let $i: \operatorname{Weil}_{\mathbb R}(S^0)\rightarrow \operatorname{Weil}_{\mathbb R}(S)$ be the natural isomorphism. Then we may define
$$\operatorname{Diff}_{S}(\mathcal{F},B,{\bf{M}},t):=i_*\operatorname{Diff}_{S^0}(\mathcal{F}|_{X^0},B|_{X^0},{\bf{M}}|_{X^0},t).$$
All the properties (1-5) follow by construction.

Write $\bm{v}=(b_1,\dots,b_l,c_1,\dots,c_m,\mu_1,\dots,\mu_n)$. By Proposition~\ref{prop: explicit formula},
$$\operatorname{mult}_DB_S(\bm{v},s)=\frac{1}{r}\left(s(a+\epsilon(r-1))+\sum_{i=1}^lp_ib_i+(1-s)\left(r-1+\sum_{k=1}^mq_kc_k\right)+\sum_{j=1}^n\lambda_j\mu_j\right)$$
for any $s\in [0,1]$.

(1) In this case,
$$1\geq \frac{1}{1-t}\operatorname{mult}_DB_S(\bm{v},t)=\frac{r-1+\frac{t}{1-t}a+\frac{1}{1-t}\left(\sum_{i=1}^lp_ib_i+\sum_{j=1}^n\lambda_j\mu_j\right)+\sum_{k=1}^mq_kc_k}{r}.$$
The rest are elementary computations.

(2) We first assume that $a=0$. In this case, by Lemma~\ref{lem: CS25 3.13(4) general case}~(3)(4) when $S$ is $\mathcal{F}$-invariant and by Lemma~\ref{lem: restriction ii} when $S$ is not $\mathcal{F}$-invariant, we see that $S$ is the only possible $\mathcal{F}$-invariant divisor which contains $D$, so $q_k=0$ for any $k$. Therefore,
$$1\geq\operatorname{mult}_DB_S(\bm{v},t)=\frac{1}{r}\left(r-1+\sum_{i=1}^lp_ib_i+\sum_{j=1}^n\lambda_j\mu_j\right)$$
and the rest are elementary computations. 

Now we assume that $a>0$. Then $a\geq 1$. In this case, since ${\mathfrak{A}}(\bm{v},t)$ is lc, by \cite[Proposition~3.3]{Cas+24}, ${\mathfrak{A}}(\bm{v},0)$ is lc, so
$$1\geq\operatorname{mult}_DB_S(\bm{v},0)=\frac{1}{r}\left(r-1+\sum_{i=1}^lp_ib_i+\sum_{k=1}^mq_kc_k+\sum_{j=1}^n\lambda_j\mu_j\right).$$
Therefore, $\sum_{k=1}^mq_kc_k\leq 1\leq a$, so
$$1\geq\operatorname{mult}_DB_S(\bm{v},t)=\frac{1}{r}\left(r+t(a-1)-(1-t)\left(1-\sum_{k=1}^mq_kc_k\right)+\sum_{i=1}^lp_ib_i+\sum_{j=1}^n\lambda_j\mu_j\right)$$
and the rest are elementary computations.

We may assume that $0,1\in\Gamma$. By \cite[Theorem~6.0.1]{CHLX23}, we may assume that $t<1$. If ${\mathfrak{A}}$ is $\mathbb Q$-factorial qdlt, then ${\mathfrak{A}}_S$ is lc by \cite[Theorem~1.8]{Cas+24}, and the theorem follows from Theorem~\ref{thm: dcc precise adjunction}. For the general case, by \cite[Theorem~1.9]{Cas+24}, we may let $h\colon {\mathfrak{A}}'\rightarrow{\mathfrak{A}}$ be a $\mathbb Q$-factorial qdlt modification of ${\mathfrak{A}}$, $S':=h^{-1}_*\widetilde{S}$, and $h_S: S'\rightarrow S$ the induced birational morphism. Let ${\mathfrak{A}}_{S'}$ be the adjoint foliated structure induced by adjunction $K_{{\mathfrak{A}}_{S'}}:=K_{{\mathfrak{A}}'}|_{S'}$. Then we have
$$K_{{\mathfrak{A}}_S}=(h_S)_*K_{{\mathfrak{A}}_{S'}}.$$
The general case now follows from the $\mathbb Q$-factorial qdlt case.

Let $\pi: X\rightarrow U$ be a contraction between normal quasi-projective varieties and ${\bf{M}}$ a nef$/U$ $\bm{b}$-divisor on $X$. Let $F$ be a general fiber of $\pi$. Assume that ${\bf{M}}_X|_F\equiv 0$. Then ${\bf{M}}|_F\equiv \bm{0}$.

nodes.statement: We may assume that dim X>dim U. Let f: Yrightarrow X be a projective birational morphism such that bfM descends to Y. Since F is a general fiber of pi, there exists a general fiber F_Y of picirc f: Yrightarrow U such that f(F_Y)=F. Let g: F_Yrightarrow F be the induced birational morphism. We have g_*(bfM_Y|_F_Y)=bfM_X|_Fequiv 0. Since bfM_Y|_F_Y is nef/U, bfM_Y|_F_Y is nef/F. By the negativity lemma, we have bfM_Y|_F_Y=g^*(bfM_X|_F)-Eequiv -E for some Egeq 0. Thus E=0, hence bfM_Y|_F_Y=g^*(bfM_X|_F)equiv 0. Since bfM|_F=overlinebfM_Y|_F_Y, it follows that bfM|_Fequivbm0.

We may assume that $\dim X>\dim U$. Let $f: Y\rightarrow X$ be a projective birational morphism such that ${\bf{M}}$ descends to $Y$. Since $F$ is a general fiber of $\pi$, there exists a general fiber $F_Y$ of $\pi\circ f: Y\rightarrow U$ 
such that $f(F_Y)=F$. Let $g: F_Y\rightarrow F$ be the induced birational morphism. We have
$$g_*({\bf{M}}_Y|_{F_Y})={\bf{M}}_X|_F\equiv 0.$$
Since ${\bf{M}}_Y|_{F_Y}$ is nef$/U$, ${\bf{M}}_Y|_{F_Y}$ is nef$/F$. By the negativity lemma, we have
$${\bf{M}}_Y|_{F_Y}=g^*({\bf{M}}_X|_F)-E\equiv -E$$
for some $E\geq 0$. Thus $E=0$, hence 
$${\bf{M}}_Y|_{F_Y}=g^*({\bf{M}}_X|_F)\equiv 0.$$ 
Since ${\bf{M}}|_F=\overline{{\bf{M}}_Y|_{F_Y}}$, it follows that ${\bf{M}}|_F\equiv\bm{0}$.

Since $S$ is not a component of $D$ and is an lc place of ${\mathfrak{B}}'$,
$S$ is a component of $\lfloor B\rfloor$.
We may write $$B=S+\sum b_{i}B_{i}+\sum c_{l}C_{l}$$
and
$$D^{\operatorname{ninv}}=\sum d_{i}B_{i},D^{\operatorname{inv}}=\sum e_{l}C_{l}$$
where $b_{i},c_{l},d_{i},e_{l}\geq 0$ and $S,B_{i},C_{l}$ are distinct prime divisors.

For any prime divisor $P$ on $S$, let $r_{P}$ be the local Cartier index of $X$ near the generic point of $P$,
$p_{i,P}:=r_{P}\operatorname{mult}_{P}(B_{i}|_{S})$, $q_{l,P}:=r_{P}\operatorname{mult}_{P}(C_{l}|_{S})$, $\lambda_{j,P}:=r_{P}\operatorname{mult}_{P}({\bf{M}}_{j,X}|_{S}-{\bf{M}}_{j,S}^S)$, $\xi_{k,P}:=r_{P}\operatorname{mult}_{P}({\bf{N}}_{k,X}|_{S}-{\bf{N}}_{k,S}^S)$, and $a_{P}$ the unique non-negative integer such that
$$(K_{\mathcal{F}}+\epsilon_{\mathcal{F}}(S)S)|_{S}=K_{\mathcal{F}_{S}}+\frac{a_{P}+\epsilon_{\mathcal{F}_{S}}(P)(r_{P}-1)}{r_{P}}P$$
near the generic point of $P$ and whose existence is guaranteed by Lemma~\ref{lem: CS25 3.13(4) general case}. Then by Proposition~\ref{prop: explicit formula}, we have
\begin{align*}
    &(tK_{\mathcal{F}}+(1-t)K_{X}+(B+D)^{\operatorname{ninv}}+(1-t)(B+D)^{\operatorname{inv}}+{\bf{M}}_{X}+{\bf{N}}_{X})|_{S}\\
    =&tK_{\mathcal{F}_{S}}+(1-t)K_{S}\\
    +&\sum_{P}\frac{1}{r_{P}}\Bigg(t(a_{P}+\epsilon_{\mathcal{F}_{S}}(P)(r_{P}-1))+\sum p_{i,P}(b_{i}+d_{i})\\
    +&(1-t)\left(r_{P}-1+\sum q_{l,P}(c_{l}+e_{l})\right)+\sum \lambda_{j,P}\mu_{j}+\sum\xi_{k,P}\nu_k\Bigg)P\\
    +&\sum \mu_{j}{\bf{M}}^S_{j,S}+\sum \nu_{k}{\bf{N}}^S_{k,S}.
\end{align*}
We have the following.
\begin{itemize}
\item By our assumption (9), if $d_i\neq0$ (resp. $e_j\neq0$), then $B_i|_S\neq0$ (resp. $C_j|_S\neq0$) over the generic point of $Z$, hence $p_{i,P}\neq0$ (resp. $q_{j,P}\neq0$) for some $P$ that is horizontal$/Z$.
\item By Theorem~\ref{thm: dcc precise adjunction}, the following set
$$\{a_P,p_{i,P}(b_i+d_i),q_{l,P}(c_l+e_l),\xi_{k,P}\nu_k\mid P\text{ is horizontal}/Z\}$$
is a subset of a finite set depending only on $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma_0$.
\item For any $k$ such that $({\bf{N}}_{k,X}|_S)|_F\not\equiv 0$, we have
$$\sum_P \frac{\xi_{k,P}\nu_k}{r_P}P|_F+\nu_k{\bf{N}}_{k,S}^S|_F=\left(\sum_P \frac{\xi_{k,P}\nu_k}{r_P}P+\nu_k{\bf{N}}_{k,S}^S\right)\Bigg|_F=({\bf{N}}_{k,X}|_S)|_F\not\equiv0,$$
so either $\xi_{k,P}\neq0$ for some $P$ that is horizontal$/Z$, or ${\bf{N}}_{k,S}^S|_F\not\equiv0$ for some $k$. In the latter case, ${\bf{N}}_{k}^S|_F\not\equiv\bm{0}$ by Lemma~\ref{lem: non-trivial of b-divisors}, so $\nu_k\in\Gamma_0$.
\end{itemize}
These indicate that, for any $i$ (resp. $l,k$) such that $d_i\neq0$ (resp. $e_l\neq0$, $({\bf{N}}_{k,X}|_S)|_F\not\equiv0$), $d_i$ (resp. $e_l,\nu_k$) belong to a finite set. The theorem follows.

We write ${\mathfrak{B}}=(X,\mathcal{F},B,{\bf{M}})(t)$ and ${\mathfrak{B}}'=(X,\mathcal{F},B',{\bf{M}}')(t')$. 

We first prove the lemma when $t=t'$. In this case, $(X,\mathcal{F},B,{\bf{M}})(t)$ is lc, $(B-B')^{\operatorname{ninv}}+(1-t)(B-B')^{\operatorname{inv}}\geq 0$, ${\bf{M}}-{\bf{M}}'$ is nef$/U$, and $(B-B')^{\operatorname{ninv}}+(1-t)(B-B')^{\operatorname{inv}}+({\bf{M}}_X-{\bf{M}}'_X)$ is $\mathbb R$-Cartier. By Lemma~\ref{lem: neg lem for generalized boundary},
$$a(D,{\mathfrak{B}})\leq a(D,{\mathfrak{B}}')$$
for any prime divisor $D$ over $X$, and the lemma follows. Therefore, in the following, we may assume that $t>t'$. 

We first prove (1). We have $1>t>t'$. The proof is very similar to \cite[Proof of Proposition~3.3]{Cas+24}. We have $t=s\cdot 1+(1-s)\cdot t'$ where $s=\frac{t-t'}{1-t'}$. Write
$${\mathfrak{A}}:=\log{\mathfrak{B}}:=(X,\mathcal{F},\Delta,{\bf{M}},t),\quad {\mathfrak{A}}':=\log{\mathfrak{B}}':=(X,\mathcal{F},\Delta',{\bf{M}}',t').$$
Let $s:=\frac{t-t'}{1-t'}$. Then $t=s\cdot 1+(1-s)\cdot t'$. Let $\Delta''$ be the unique $\mathbb R$-divisor such that $s\Delta''+(1-s)\Delta'=\Delta$ and let ${\bf{M}}''$ be the unique $\bm{b}$-divisor such that $s{\bf{M}}''+(1-s){\bf{M}}'={\bf{M}}$. Since ${\mathfrak{B}}/U\geq{\mathfrak{B}}'/U$,
$${\bf{M}}''-{\bf{M}}=\frac{1-s}{s}({\bf{M}}-{\bf{M}}')$$
is nef$/U$. Hence ${\bf{M}}''$ is nef$/U$ as well. Since
$$\Delta^{\operatorname{ninv}}+\frac{1}{1-t}\Delta^{\operatorname{inv}}\geq\Delta'^{\operatorname{ninv}}+\frac{1}{1-t'}\Delta'^{\operatorname{inv}},$$
we have 
$$\Delta''=\frac{1}{s}(\Delta-(1-s)\Delta')\geq 0\text{ and }\Delta''^{\operatorname{ninv}}\geq\Delta^{\operatorname{ninv}}.$$
We let ${\mathfrak{A}}'':=(X,\mathcal{F},\Delta'',{\bf{M}}'')$ and let $h\colon (Y,\mathcal{F}_Y,B_Y'',{\bf{M}}'';G)\rightarrow (X,\mathcal{F},\Delta'',{\bf{M}}'')$ be a $\mathbb Q$-factorial proper ACSS modification of $(X,\mathcal{F},\Delta'',{\bf{M}}'')$ (cf.~\cite[Theorem~8.2.2]{CHLX23}). We have
$$B_Y''=h^{-1}_*(\Delta''^{\operatorname{ninv}}\wedge\operatorname{Supp} \Delta''^{\operatorname{ninv}})+\operatorname{Exc}(h)^{\operatorname{ninv}},$$
and for any $h$-exceptional prime divisor $E$, we have
$$a(E,{\mathfrak{A}}'')\leq -\epsilon_{\mathcal{F}}(E),$$
since $h$ is an ACSS modification of ${\mathfrak{A}}''$ and only extracts nklt places of ${\mathfrak{A}}''$. 
Since ${\mathfrak{A}}$ is lc, we have
$$a(E,{\mathfrak{A}})\geq -t\epsilon_{\mathcal{F}}(E)-(1-t).$$
Since ${\mathfrak{A}}=s{\mathfrak{A}}''+(1-s){\mathfrak{A}}'$, we have
$$a(E,{\mathfrak{A}})=sa(E,{\mathfrak{A}}'')+(1-s)a(E,{\mathfrak{A}}').$$
Thus
$$a(E,{\mathfrak{A}}')\geq\frac{-t\epsilon_{\mathcal{F}}(E)-(1-t)+s\epsilon_{\mathcal{F}}(E)}{1-s}=-t'\epsilon_{\mathcal{F}}(E)-(1-t')$$
and equality holds if and only if $a(E,{\mathfrak{A}}'')=-\epsilon_{\mathcal{F}}(E)$ and $a(E,{\mathfrak{A}})=-t\epsilon_{\mathcal{F}}(E)-(1-t)$. Let 
$${\mathfrak{B}}_{Y}':=(Y,\mathcal{F}_Y,B_{Y}':=h^{-1}_*B'+\operatorname{Exc}(h),{\bf{M}}')(t'),{\mathfrak{B}}_Y:=(Y,\mathcal{F}_Y,B_{Y}:=h^{-1}_*B+\operatorname{Exc}(h),{\bf{M}})(t).$$
Then we have 
$$K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_{Y}'}\geq h^*K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'}\quad \text{ and }\quad K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_Y}\geq h^*K_{{\mathfrak{B}}}.$$
\begin{claim}\label{claim: by+g and by'}
$B_Y''+G\geq B_{Y}\geq B_Y'$.
\end{claim}
\begin{proof}
    For any prime divisor $D$ that is an irreducible component of $B_Y$, we distinguish four cases.
    \medskip

    \noindent\textbf{Case 1.} $D$ is an irreducible component of $\operatorname{Exc}(h)^{\operatorname{inv}}$. Then
    $$\operatorname{mult}_DB_{Y}=1=\operatorname{mult}_DG=\operatorname{mult}_D(B_Y''+G).$$
    
    \medskip

    \noindent\textbf{Case 2.} $D$ is an irreducible component of $\operatorname{Exc}(h)^{\operatorname{ninv}}$. Then
    $$\operatorname{mult}_DB_{Y}=1=\operatorname{mult}_DB_Y''=\operatorname{mult}_D(B_Y''+G).$$

    \medskip

    \noindent\textbf{Case 3.} $D$ is an irreducible component of $h^{-1}_*B$ that is $\mathcal{F}_Y$-invariant. Then
$$\operatorname{mult}_D(B_Y''+G)=\operatorname{mult}_DG=1\geq\operatorname{mult}_{h_*D}B=\operatorname{mult}_DB_{Y}.$$

    \medskip

    \noindent\textbf{Case 4.} $D$ is an irreducible component of $h^{-1}_*B$ that is not $\mathcal{F}_Y$-invariant. Then
    $$\operatorname{mult}_D(B_Y''+G)=\operatorname{mult}_DB_Y''=\min\{\operatorname{mult}_{h_*D}\Delta''^{\operatorname{ninv}},1\}\geq\operatorname{mult}_{h_*D}\Delta^{\operatorname{ninv}}=\operatorname{mult}_DB_{Y}.$$
    The claim follows.
\end{proof}
\noindent\textit{Proof of Lemma~\ref{lem: lc preserved under inequality} continued.} We let
$${\mathfrak{B}}_Y(s):=(Y,\mathcal{F}_Y,B_Y''+G,{\bf{M}}'')(s)$$
for any $s\in [0,1]$. Then ${\mathfrak{B}}_Y(s)$ is $\mathbb Q$-factorial lc for any $s\in [0,1]$. By Claim~\ref{claim: by+g and by'}, ${\mathfrak{B}}_Y(t')/U\geq{\mathfrak{B}}_Y'/U$. By the $t=t'$ case, ${\mathfrak{B}}_{Y}'$ is lc, hence ${\mathfrak{B}}'$ is lc. This implies (1).

Now we prove (2). We let $g: V\rightarrow X$ be a $\mathbb Q$-factorial qdlt modification of ${\mathfrak{B}}$ and let ${\mathfrak{B}}_V:=g^*{\mathfrak{B}}:=(V,\mathcal{F}_V,B_V,{\bf{M}})(t)$. Then $B_V=g^{-1}_*B+\operatorname{Exc}(g)$. By (1), we have that ${\mathfrak{B}}_V(s):=(V,\mathcal{F}_V,B_V,{\bf{M}})(s)$ is lc for any $s\in [0,t]$. Since
$${\mathfrak{B}}_V(s)={\mathfrak{B}}_V^{\frac{s}{t}}\cdot{\mathfrak{B}}_V(0)^{\frac{t-s}{t}},$$
for any $s\in (0,t]$, any lc place of ${\mathfrak{B}}_V(s)$ is an lc place of ${\mathfrak{B}}_V$. Since $B\geq B'$, $B_V\geq g^{-1}_*B'+\operatorname{Exc}(g)$, so any lc place of ${\mathfrak{B}}'$ is an lc place of ${\mathfrak{B}}_V(t')$ and hence an lc place of ${\mathfrak{B}}_V$, hence an lc place of ${\mathfrak{B}}$. (2) follows.

Let $E_0$ be an lc place of ${\mathfrak{B}}^{\mu}$. Let $f: W\rightarrow X$ be a foliated log resolution of ${\mathfrak{B}}$ such that $E_0$ is on $W$. Let $E_0,\dots,E_n$ be all the $f$-exceptional prime divisors and let ${\mathfrak{B}}_W(s):=(f^{-1}_*{\mathfrak{B}}^s,\operatorname{Exc}(f))$. Then we have
$$K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_W(s)}=f^*K_{{\mathfrak{B}}^s}+\sum_{i=0}^nb(i,s)E_i\sim_{\mathbb R,X}\sum_{i=0}^nb(i,s)E_i$$
for some real numbers $b(i,s)$. By Lemma~\ref{lem: klt bs}, ${\mathfrak{B}}^s$ is klt for any $s\in [0,\mu)$, hence $b(i,s)>0$ for any $i$ and any $s\in [0,\mu)$. Since ${\mathfrak{B}}^\mu$ is lc and $E_0$ is an lc place of ${\mathfrak{B}}^{\mu}$,
$b(i,\mu)\geq 0$ and $b(0,\mu)=0$. 

We run a $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_W(\mu)}$-MMP$/X$ with scaling of an ample divisor. By \cite[Theorem~3.6]{Cas+25b}, this MMP terminates with a good minimal model ${\mathfrak{B}}_V(\mu)/X$ of ${\mathfrak{B}}_W(\mu)/X$ such that $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_V(\mu)}\sim_{\mathbb R,X}0$ and the divisors contracted by the induced birational map $\phi\colon W\dashrightarrow V$ are exactly the $E_i$ such that $b(i,\mu)>0$. In particular, $E_0$ is not contracted by $\phi$. Possibly reordering indices, we may assume that $E_i$ is not contracted by $\phi$ if and only if $i\leq m$ for some $m\leq n$. We let $E_{i,V}$ be the images of $E_i$ on $V$ for any $0\leq i\leq n$ and let $\pi: V\rightarrow X$ be the induced morphism. Let ${\mathfrak{B}}_V(s):=\phi_*{\mathfrak{B}}_W(s)$ for any $s\in [0,1]$. Then ${\mathfrak{B}}_V(\mu)=\pi^*{\mathfrak{B}}^{\mu}$ is $\mathbb Q$-factorial qdlt. 

Since $\phi$ is also a sequence of steps of a $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_W(s)}$-MMP$/U$ for any $0\leq \mu-s\ll 1$, ${\mathfrak{B}}_V(s)$ is $\mathbb Q$-factorial qdlt for any $0\leq \mu-s\ll 1$. Now pick $s_0$ such that $0<\mu-s_0\ll 1$ and run a $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_V(s_0)}$-MMP$/X$. Note that
$$K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_V(s_0)}\sim_{\mathbb R,X}\sum_{i=0}^mb(i,s_0)E_{i,V}.$$
Since $b(i,s_0)>0$ for any $i$, by \cite[Theorem~3.6]{Cas+25b} and since $X$ is $\mathbb Q$-factorial klt, this MMP terminates with ${\mathfrak{B}}^{s_0}/X$ as a good minimal model of ${\mathfrak{B}}_V(s_0)/X$, and the last step of this MMP is a divisorial contraction $g: Y\rightarrow X$. We let ${\mathfrak{B}}_Y(s)$ be the pushforward of ${\mathfrak{B}}_V(s)$ on $Y$ for any $s\in [0,1]$ and let $E$ be the unique prime $g$-exceptional divisor. Then we have ${\mathfrak{B}}_Y(s)=(g^{-1}_*{\mathfrak{B}}^s,E)$ for any $s\in [0,1]$.

We show that $g$ satisfies our requirements. 

(1) follows from our construction. 

Since $\pi$ only extracts lc places of ${\mathfrak{B}}^{\mu}$, $g$ only extracts lc places of ${\mathfrak{B}}^{\mu}$. This implies (2).

To prove (3), note that by our construction, ${\mathfrak{B}}_Y(s_0)$ is $\mathbb Q$-factorial qdlt and $E$ is the only lc place of ${\mathfrak{B}}_Y(s_0)$, so ${\mathfrak{B}}_Y(s_0)$ is $\mathbb Q$-factorial plt. By the definition of qdlt \cite[Definition~3.1]{Cas+24}, ${\mathfrak{B}}_Y(0)$ is plt. Since $E$ is an lc place of ${\mathfrak{B}}_Y(0)$, $E$ is normal. For any $s\in [0,\mu)$, since ${\mathfrak{B}}_Y(\mu)\geq{\mathfrak{B}}_Y(s)$, ${\mathfrak{B}}_Y(s)$ is lc. If ${\mathfrak{B}}_Y(s)$ is not plt for some $s\in (0,\mu)$, then there exists an lc place $F\neq E$ of ${\mathfrak{B}}_Y(s)$. By Lemma~\ref{lem: lc preserved under inequality}, $F$ is an lc place of ${\mathfrak{B}}_Y(r)$ for any $r\in [s,\mu]$. Since $r\mapsto a(F,{\mathfrak{B}}_Y(r))$ is a quadratic function, 
$F$ is an lc place of ${\mathfrak{B}}_Y(r)$ for any $r\in [0,\mu]$. Thus $F$ is an lc place of ${\mathfrak{B}}_Y(s_0)$, which is not possible. This implies (3).

By Proposition~\ref{prop: when fiber bounded} we may assume that $\dim F \geq 2$. By Lemma~\ref{lem: no part 2 case}, we may assume that $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}(s)}\not\sim_{\mathbb R,U}0$ for any $s\neq t$.

Let $\widetilde S$ be an irreducible component of $\lfloor B\rfloor$. Since all the irreducible components of $B$ are horizontal$/U$ and ample$/U$, $\widetilde S$ is horizontal$/U$ and ample$/U$. Let $S$ be the normalization of $\widetilde S$, ${\bf{M}}_j^S:={\bf{M}}_j|_S$ for any $j$, and ${\bf{M}}^S:={\bf{M}}|_S$. Since $d_F\geq 2$, we have the following.
\begin{itemize}
 \item ${\bf{M}}_{j,X}|_S$ is ample$/U$, hence ${\bf{M}}_{j,X}|_S\not\equiv_U0$ for any $j$.
 \item For any irreducible component $L\neq S$ of $B$, $L|_S\geq 0$ is ample$/U$, hence $L|_S\neq0$ over the generic point of $U$.
\end{itemize}
Let $\mathfrak{C}(s):=\left(X,\mathcal{F},\widetilde{S},\bm{0}\right)(s)$ for any $s\in [0,1]$. Then ${\mathfrak{B}}(s)/U\geq\mathfrak{C}(s)/U$ for any $s\in [0,1]$. Since ${\mathfrak{B}}(t)$ is lc, by Lemma~\ref{lem: lc preserved under inequality}, ${\mathfrak{B}}(s)$ and $\mathfrak{C}(s)$ are lc for any $s\in [0,t]$. We let $h\colon X'\rightarrow X$ be a $\mathbb Q$-factorial qdlt modification of $\mathfrak{C}\left(\frac{t}{2}\right)$ and let $${\mathfrak{B}}'(s):=(h^{-1}_*{\mathfrak{B}}(s),\operatorname{Exc}(h)),\quad \mathfrak{C}'(s):=(h^{-1}_*\mathfrak{C}(s),\operatorname{Exc}(h))$$ for any $s\in [0,1]$. By Lemma~\ref{lem: lc preserved under inequality} and linearity of discrepancies, any prime divisor extracted by $h$ is an lc place of $\mathfrak{C}(s)$ and ${\mathfrak{B}}(s)$ for any $s\in [0,t]$. In particular, ${\mathfrak{B}}'(s)=h^*{\mathfrak{B}}(s)$ and $\mathfrak{C}'(s)=h^*\mathfrak{C}(s)$ for any $s\in [0,1]$. Let $S':=h^{-1}_*\widetilde{S}$. Since $\mathfrak{C}\left(\frac{t}{2}\right)$ is $\mathbb Q$-factorial qdlt, $(X',S'+\operatorname{Exc}(h))$ is $\mathbb Q$-factorial qdlt. In particular, $S'$ is normal. 

Let $h_S: S'\rightarrow S$ be the induced birational morphism. Write ${\mathfrak{B}}'(s):=(X',\mathcal{F}',B',{\bf{M}})(s)$ where $B'=h^{-1}_*B+\operatorname{Exc}(h)$. Then for any irreducible component $L'\neq S'$ of $B'$ that is not an irreducible component of $\operatorname{Exc}(h)$, $h_*L'$ is an irreducible component of $B$. Since $(X,B,{\bf{M}})$ is lc, $h_*L'$ does not contain any lc center of $(X,S)$. Since $h$ only extracts lc places of $(X,S)$,
$$L'|_{S'}=h_S^*\left((h_*L')|_{S}\right)$$
is big$/U$ and nef$/U$. Moreover, for any $j$,
$${\bf{M}}_{j,X'}|_{S'}=h_S^*\left({\bf{M}}_{j,X}|_S\right)=h_S^*h_{S,*}\left({\bf{M}}_{j,X'}|_{S'}\right)$$

By Theorem~\ref{thm: dcc precise adjunction}, either $t$ belongs to a finite set depending only on $d$ and $\Gamma$, or $B_{S'}(t)=B_{S'}(s)$ for any $s\in [0,1)$. In the latter case, we let

We may assume that $1\in\Gamma$. By Lemma~\ref{lem: no part 2 case}, we may assume that $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}(s)}\not\sim_{\mathbb R,U}0$ for any $s\neq t$. By condition (4) of Set-up~\ref{setup: global acc}, $t<1$.

Let $E$ be an lc place of ${\mathfrak{B}}$ such that $V:=\operatorname{center}_XE$ is horizontal$/U$. 
By Lemma~\ref{lem: when exist lc place}, we may assume that $E$ is exceptional$/X$. Since $X$ is klt, by \cite[Theorem~2.2.3]{Cas+25a}, there exists a projective birational morphism $h\colon X'\rightarrow X$ such that $X'$ is $\mathbb Q$-factorial and $\operatorname{Exc}(h)=E$. We write
$${\mathfrak{B}}'(s):=(h^{-1}_*{\mathfrak{B}}(s),E):=(X',\mathcal{F}',B',{\bf{M}})(s)$$
for any $s\in [0,1]$ and let ${\mathfrak{B}}':={\mathfrak{B}}'(t)$.

By Lemma~\ref{lem: acc implies precise acc} and Theorem~\ref{thm: acc lct general version}, Theorem~\ref{thm: ACC precise} holds in dimension $d$. Let $\Gamma':=\operatorname{lct}_{{\operatorname{aif}}}(d,\Gamma\cup\mathbb N)$ be the ACC set as in Theorem~\ref{thm: acc lct general version} and let $\Gamma_1:=\Gamma\cap\Gamma'$. Then $\Gamma_1$ is a finite set. By Theorem~\ref{thm: ACC precise} in dimension $d$, we have the following.
\begin{itemize}
    \item For any irreducible component $D$ of $B$, either $\operatorname{mult}_DB\in\Gamma_1$ or $V\not\subset\operatorname{Supp} D$. In the latter case, $h^*D=h^{-1}_*D$ is big$/U$.
    \item For any $j$, either $\mu_j\in\Gamma_1$, or $h^*{\bf{M}}_{j,X}={\bf{M}}_{j,X'}$. In the latter case, ${\bf{M}}_{j,X'}$ is big$/U$.
    \item Either $t\in\Gamma_1$, or ${\mathfrak{B}}(s)$ is lc for some $s>t$. In the latter case, by Lemma~\ref{lem: lc preserved under inequality} and linearity of discrepancies, we have that $E$ is an lc place of ${\mathfrak{B}}(s)$ for any $s\in [0,1]$, and ${\mathfrak{B}}'(s)=h^*{\mathfrak{B}}(s)$ for any $s\in [0,1]$, hence $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'(s)}$ is big$/U$ or anti-big$/U$ for any $s\in [0,1]$ such that $s\neq t$.
\end{itemize}
We run a $(K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'}-\delta E)$-MMP$/U$ with scaling of an ample divisor for some $0<\delta\ll 1$. Since $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'}=h^*K_{{\mathfrak{B}}}\sim_{\mathbb R,U}0$, this is a $(-E)$-MMP$/U$ so $E$ is not contracted by this MMP. By \cite[Theorem~2.1.5]{Cas+25a}, the MMP terminates with a Mori fiber space$/U$ $g: X''\rightarrow T$ associated with a birational map$/U$ $\phi\colon X'\dashrightarrow X''$. Let $E'':=\phi_*E$, then $E''$ is ample$/T$. Let ${\mathfrak{B}}''(s):=\phi_*{\mathfrak{B}}'(s)$ for any $s\in [0,1]$. Since $\phi$ is $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'}$-trivial, ${\mathfrak{B}}''(t)$ is lc. Since $X'$ is $\mathbb Q$-factorial klt, $X''$ is $\mathbb Q$-factorial klt.

Let $B''$ be the horizontal$/T$ part of $\phi_*B'$ and let $${\bf{N}}:=\sum_{j\mid {\bf{M}}_{j,X''}\not\sim_{\mathbb R,T}0}\mu_j{\bf{M}}_j.$$ 
Let
$$\mathfrak{C}(s):=(X'',\mathcal{F}'':=\phi_*\mathcal{F}',B'',{\bf{N}})(s)$$
for any $s\in [0,1]$. Then ${\mathfrak{B}}''(s)\geq\mathfrak{C}(s)$ for any $s\in [0,1]$. Since ${\mathfrak{B}}''(t)$ is lc, by Lemma~\ref{lem: lc preserved under inequality}, $\mathfrak{C}(t)$ is lc. Since $\rho(X''/T)=1$,
$$K_{\mathfrak{C}(s)}\sim_{\mathbb R,T}K_{{\mathfrak{B}}''(s)}$$
for any $s\in [0,1]$. In particular, 
$$K_{\mathfrak{C}(t)}\sim_{\mathbb R,T}K_{{\mathfrak{B}}''(t)}\sim_{\mathbb R,T}0.$$

For any irreducible component $D$ of $B$ (resp. any $j$, $t$), either $\operatorname{mult}_DB\in\Gamma_1$ (resp. $\mu_j\in\Gamma_1$, $t\in\Gamma_1$), or $h^{-1}_*D$ is big$/U$ (resp. ${\bf{M}}_{j,X'}$ is big$/U$, $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'(s)}$ is big$/U$ or anti-big$/U$ for any $s\in [0,1]$ such that $s\neq t$). In the latter case, $\phi_*h^{-1}_*D$ is big$/U$ (resp. ${\bf{M}}_{j,X''}$ is big$/U$, $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}''(s)}$ is big$/U$ or anti-big$/U$ for any $s\in [0,1]$ such that $s\neq t$), hence $\phi_*h^{-1}_*D$ is ample$/T$ (resp.  ${\bf{M}}_{j,X''}$ is ample$/T$, $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}''(s)}$ is ample$/T$ or anti-ample$/T$ for any $s\in [0,1]$ such that $t\neq s$), so $\phi_*h^{-1}_*D$ is an irreducible component of $B''$ (resp. ${\bf{M}}_{j,X''}\not\sim_{\mathbb R,T}0$, $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}''(s)}\not\sim_{\mathbb R,T}0$ for any $s\in [0,1]$ such that $t\neq s$). There are two cases.

\medskip

\noindent\textbf{Case 1.} We have $K_{\mathfrak{C}(s)}\not\sim_{\mathbb R,T}0$ for some $s\neq t$. Then, since $\rho(X''/T)=1$, we have that $K_{\mathfrak{C}(s)}\not\sim_{\mathbb R,T}0$ for any $s\neq t$. By Lemma~\ref{lem: when exist lc place} applied to $\mathfrak{C}(t)$ and $g: X''\rightarrow T$, there exists a finite set $\Gamma_2$ depending only on $d$ and $\Gamma$ such that $B'',t\in\Gamma_2$ and $\mu_j\in\Gamma_2$ for any $j$ such that ${\bf{M}}_{j,X''}\not\sim_{\mathbb R,T}0$. Thus $B,t,\mu_1,\dots,\mu_n\in\Gamma_1\cup\Gamma_2$ and we are done.

\medskip

\noindent\textbf{Case 2.} We have $K_{\mathfrak{C}(s)}\sim_{\mathbb R,T}0$ for some $s\neq t$, hence $K_{\mathfrak{C}(s)}\sim_{\mathbb R,T}0$ for any $s\neq t$. Thus $t\in\Gamma_1$. By Lemma~\ref{lem: no part 2 case}, there exists a finite set $\Gamma_2$ depending only on $d$ and $\Gamma$ such that $B'',t\in\Gamma_2$ and $\mu_j\in\Gamma_2$ for any $j$ such that ${\bf{M}}_{j,X''}\not\sim_{\mathbb R,T}0$. Thus $B,t,\mu_1,\dots,\mu_n\in\Gamma_1\cup\Gamma_2$ and we are done.

$${\mathfrak{D}}_i(\mu,s):=(X_i'',\mathcal{F}_i'',B_i''^o+\mu E_i'',{\bf{N}}^i)(s)$$
for any $\mu,s\in [0,1]$. Then we have
$$K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(e_i,s)}\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_i''(s)}$$
for any $s\in [0,1]$. Since ${\mathfrak{B}}_i''(t_i')$ is klt, ${\mathfrak{D}}_i(e_i,t_i')$ is klt. Since $\tau<\tau_{\operatorname{ilct}}(d,\Gamma)$ and $\lim_{i\rightarrow+\infty}e_i=1$, possibly passing to a subsequence and applying Lemma~\ref{lem: lc preserved under inequality}, we may assume that for any $\mu\in [0,1]$ and any $s\in [0,t_i]$, ${\mathfrak{D}}_i(\mu,s)$ is lc. Moreover, if we are in \textbf{Case 1}, then ${\mathfrak{D}}_i(\mu,s)$ is lc for any $\mu,s\in [0,1]$.


\medskip

\noindent\textbf{Step 3.} We prove the theorem when $b_{i,1}$ is strictly increasing and $\lim_{i\rightarrow+\infty}b_{i,1}=1$. In the rest of this step, we assume that $\lim_{i\rightarrow+\infty}b_{i,1}=1$.

We let $B'_{i,1}:=h_{i,*}^{-1}B_{i,1}$, $B''_{i,1}:=\phi_{i,*}B'_{i,1}$, $\Delta_i:=B_i-b_{i,1}B_{i,1}$, $\Delta_i':=B_i'-b_{i,1}B'_{i,1}$, and $$\Delta_i'':=\phi_{i,*}\Delta_i'=B_i''-b_{i,1}B''_{i,1}.$$
Then we have
\begin{align*}
{\mathfrak{B}}_i'(s) &= (X_i',\mathcal{F}_i',b_{i,1}B'_{i,1}+\Delta_i'+e_iE_i',{\bf{M}}^i)(s),\\
{\mathfrak{B}}_i''(s) &= (X_i'',\mathcal{F}_i'',b_{i,1}B''_{i,1}+\Delta_i''+e_iE_i'',{\bf{M}}^i)(s)
\end{align*}
for any $s\in [0,1]$. We let
$$\mathfrak{C}_i(s):=(X_i,\mathcal{F}_i,B_{i,1}+\Delta_i,{\bf{M}}^i)(s),\quad \mathfrak{C}_i'(s):=(X_i',\mathcal{F}_i',B_{i,1}'+\Delta_i'+E_i,{\bf{M}}^i)(s),$$
and
$$\mathfrak{C}_i''(s):=(X_i'',\mathcal{F}_i'',B_{i,1}''+\Delta_i''+E_i'',{\bf{M}}^i)(s)$$
for any $s\in [0,1]$. Since $$\lim_{i\rightarrow+\infty}b_{i,1}=\lim_{i\rightarrow+\infty}e_i=1$$ 
and $\tau<\tau_{\operatorname{ilct}}(d,\Gamma)$, and ${\mathfrak{B}}_i(t_i'),{\mathfrak{B}}_i'(t_i'),{\mathfrak{B}}_i''(t_i')$ are klt, by definition of $\tau$ and by Theorem~\ref{thm: acc lct general version}, possibly passing to a subsequence, we have that
\begin{itemize}
    \item $\mathfrak{C}_i(s),\mathfrak{C}_i'(s),\mathfrak{C}_i''(s)$ are lc for any $s\in [1-\tau,1]=[1-t_i',1]$ if we are in \textbf{Case 1}, and
    \item $\mathfrak{C}_i(t_i'),\mathfrak{C}_i'(t_i'),\mathfrak{C}_i''(t_i')$ are lc if we are in \textbf{Case 2}. 
\end{itemize}
In particular, $\mathfrak{C}_i(t_i),\mathfrak{C}_i'(t_i),\mathfrak{C}_i''(t_i)$ are lc. Since $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_i(t_i)}\sim_{\mathbb R,U_i}0$, $B_{i,1}$ is ample$/U_i$, and ${\mathfrak{B}}_i(s)=(\mathfrak{C}_i(s),(b_{i,1}-1)B_{i,1})$ for any $s\in [0,1]$, $K_{\mathfrak{C}_i(t_i)}$ is ample$/U_i$. Since $h_i$ contracts $E_i$ and $\mathfrak{C}_i(t_i)$ is lc, we have that
$$K_{\mathfrak{C}_i'(t_i)}\geq h_i^*K_{\mathfrak{C}_i(t_i)}.$$
Therefore, $K_{\mathfrak{C}_i'(t_i)}$ is big$/U_i$. Thus $K_{\mathfrak{C}_i''(t_i)}$ is big$/U_i$. Since $\rho(X_i''/T_i)=1$, $K_{\mathfrak{C}_i''(t_i)}$ is ample$/T_i$. 
\begin{claim}\label{claim: no divisorial contraction}
    Possibly passing to a subsequence, we have that $B_{i,1}'$ is not contracted by $\phi_i$ for any $i$.
\end{claim}
\begin{proof}
    Suppose the claim does not hold. Since $\rho(X_i'/U_i)=2$, we may write $\phi_i=\psi_i\circ\varphi_i$ where $\varphi_i: X_i'\dashrightarrow Y_i$ is a sequence of flips and $\psi_i: Y_i\rightarrow X_i''$ is the divisorial contraction of $B_{Y_i,1}:=(\varphi_i)_*B_{i,1}'$. Let 
    $${\mathfrak{B}}_{Y_i}(s):=\varphi_{i,*}{\mathfrak{B}}_i'(s) \quad \text{and}\quad \mathfrak{C}_{Y_i}(s):=\varphi_{i,*}\mathfrak{C}_i'(s)$$
    for any $s\in [0,1]$. Since ${\mathfrak{B}}_i'(t_i')$ is klt and $-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_i'(t_i')}$ is semi-ample$/U_i$, ${\mathfrak{B}}_{Y_i}(t_i')$ is klt. Since $\tau<\tau_{\operatorname{ilct}}(d,\Gamma)$, by Theorem~\ref{thm: acc lct general version}, possibly passing to a subsequence, we have that $\mathfrak{C}_{Y_i}(s)$ is lc for any $t_i'\leq s\leq t_i$. Since $K_{\mathfrak{C}_i'(t_i)}$ is big$/U_i$, $K_{\mathfrak{C}_{Y_i}(t_i)}$ is big$/U_i$. Since $\psi_i$ contracts $B_{Y_i,1}$ and $\mathfrak{C}_i''(t_i)$ is lc, we have
    $$K_{\mathfrak{C}_{Y_i}(t_i)}\geq \psi_i^*K_{\mathfrak{C}_i''(t_i)}.$$
    Let $R_i$ be the unique extremal ray of $\overline{NE}(X_i'/X_i)$ and let $S_i$ be the unique extremal ray of $\overline{NE}(Y_i/X_i'')$. By the negativity lemma, $K_{\mathfrak{C}_i'(t_i)}\cdot R_i\leq 0$ and $K_{\mathfrak{C}_{Y_i}(t_i)}\cdot S_i\leq 0$. This contradicts Lemma~\ref{lem: relative two-ray}.
\end{proof}

\begin{claim}\label{claim: no trivial case}
    Possibly passing to a subsequence, we have that $B_{i,1}''$ is ample$/T_i$.
\end{claim}
\begin{proof}
Suppose the claim does not hold. By Claim~\ref{claim: no divisorial contraction}, possibly passing to a subsequence, we may assume that $B_{i,1}''\neq0$ but $B_{i,1}''$ is vertical$/T_i$ for any $i$. Since $B_{i,1}$ dominates $U_i$, $B_{i,1}''$ dominates $U_i$. Thus $\dim T_i>\dim U_i$, so $$\dim X_i-\dim T_i<\dim X_i-\dim U_i=d'.$$
We have
$$K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(1,s)}\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}K_{\mathfrak{C}_i''(s)}$$
for any $s\in [0,1]$. Let $\Gamma':=\Gamma\cup\{e_i\}_{i=1}^{+\infty}$, then $\Gamma'$ is a DCC set. 

By \textbf{Step 2}, if we are in \textbf{Case 2}, then $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(t_i,s)}\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_i''(t_i)}\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}0$. By the inductive hypothesis on $d_F$, $\{e_i\}$ is a finite set, a contradiction. Therefore, we are in \textbf{Case 1}, and we have $t_i'=1-\tau$ for each $i$. By \textbf{Step 2}, $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(e_i,1-\tau)}\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_i''(t_i')}$ is anti-ample$/T_i$.

If $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(1,1-\tau)}$ is ample$/T_i$, then there exists $e_i'\in (e_i,1)$ such that $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(e_i',1-\tau)}\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}0$. By the inductive hypothesis on $d_F$, $\{e_i'\}$ belongs to a finite set, a contradiction. Thus $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(1,1-\tau)}$ is not ample$/T_i$. Since $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(1,t_i)}\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}K_{\mathfrak{C}_i''(t_i)}$ is ample$/T_i$, there exists $t_i''\in [1-\tau,t_i)$ such that $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(1,t_i'')}\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}0$. Since $E_i''$ is an irreducible component of $\lfloor B_i''^o+E_i''\rfloor$ and $\tau<\tau_{\operatorname{aux}}(d,\Gamma)$, by Lemma~\ref{lem: one lc place one close to one}, $t_i''\not\in (1-\tau_{\operatorname{aux}}(d,\Gamma),1)$. Thus
$$1-\tau\leq t_i'\leq 1-\tau_{\operatorname{aux}}(d,\Gamma)<1-\tau,$$
a contradiction.
\end{proof}
\noindent\textit{Proof of Theorem~\ref{thm: acc to global acc} continued.} By Claims~\ref{claim: no divisorial contraction} and~\ref{claim: no trivial case}, we may assume that $B_{i,1}''$ is ample$/T_i$ for each $i$. We let $\Delta_i''^o$ be the horizontal$/T_i$ part of $\Delta_i''$ and let
$${\mathfrak{D}}_i(\lambda,\mu,s):=\left(X_i'',\mathcal{F}_i'',\Delta_i''^o+\lambda B_{i,1}''+\mu E_i'',{\bf{N}}^i\right)(s)$$
for any $\lambda,\mu,s\in [0,1]$. Then we have
$$K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(b_{i,1},e_i,s)}\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_i''(s)}\text{ and }K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(1,1,s)}\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}K_{\mathfrak{C}_i''(s)}$$
for any $s\in [0,1]$. By \textbf{Step 2}, if we are in \textbf{Case 1}, then $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(b_{i,1},e_i,t_i')}$ is anti-ample$/T_i$, and if we are in \textbf{Case 2}, then $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(b_{i,1},e_i,t_i')}\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}0$. Since $\tau<\tau_{\operatorname{ilct}}(d,\Gamma)$, possibly passing to a subsequence and applying Lemma~\ref{lem: lc preserved under inequality}, we may assume that for any $\lambda\in [0,1],\mu\in [0,1]$, and $s\in [0,t_i]$, ${\mathfrak{D}}_i(\lambda,\mu,s)$ is lc. Moreover, if we are in \textbf{Case 1}, then ${\mathfrak{D}}_i(\lambda,\mu,s)$ is lc for any $\lambda,\mu,s\in [0,1]$.

Since $\rho(X_i''/T_i)=1$, we have that
$$B_{i,1}''^{\operatorname{ninv}}+(1-t_i')B_{i,1}''^{\operatorname{inv}}\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}c_i(E_i''^{\operatorname{ninv}}+(1-t_i')E_i''^{\operatorname{inv}})$$
for some positive real number $c_i$. Possibly passing to a subsequence, we may assume that $c_i\leq 1$ for each $i$ or $c_i>1$ for each $i$. 

If $c_i\leq 1$ (resp. $c_i>1$), then we let $e_i':=e_i-\lambda_i(1-b_{i,1})$ (resp. $b_i':=b_i-\frac{1}{\lambda_i}(1-e_i)$). Possibly passing to a subsequence, we may assume that $e_i'\in (0,1)$ (resp. $b_i'\in (0,1)$) is strictly increasing and $\lim_{i\rightarrow+\infty}e_i'=1$ (resp. $\lim_{i\rightarrow+\infty}b_i'=1$). 

We have
$$K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(1,e_i',t_i')}\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(b_i,e_i,t_i')}\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_i''(t_i')}$$
$$\text{(resp. }K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(b_i',1,t_i')}\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(b_i,e_i,t_i')}\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_i''(t_i')}\text{)}.$$

If we are in \textbf{Case 2}, then $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(1,e_i',t_i')}\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}0$ (resp. $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(b_i',1,t_i')}\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}0$). If $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(1,e_i',s)}\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}0$ (resp. $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(b_i',1,s)}\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}0$) for any $s\in [0,1]$, then by Lemma~\ref{lem: no part 2 case}, $\{e_i'\}$ (resp. $\{b_i'\}$) is a finite set, a contradiction. Thus $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(1,e_i',s)}\not\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}0$ (resp. $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(b_i',1,s)}\not\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}0$) for any $s\in [0,1]$ such that $s\neq t$. By Lemma~\ref{lem: one lc place one close to one}, $e_i'<1-\tau_{\operatorname{aux}}(d,\Gamma)$ (resp. $b_i'<1-\tau_{\operatorname{aux}}(d,\Gamma)$) for any $i$. This is not possible as $\lim_{i\rightarrow+\infty}e_i'=1$ (resp. $\lim_{i\rightarrow+\infty}b_i'=1$). Therefore, we are in \textbf{Case 1}, and we have $t_i'=1-\tau$ and $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(1,e_i',1-\tau)}$ (resp. $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(b_i',1,1-\tau)}$) is anti-ample$/T_i$. 

If $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(1,1,1-\tau)}$ is ample$/T_i$ for infinitely many $i$, then possibly passing to a subsequence, we may assume that $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(1,1,1-\tau)}$ is ample$/T_i$ for each $i$. Then there exists $e_i''\in (e_i',1)$ (resp. $b_i''\in (b_i',1)$) such that $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(1,e_i'',1-\tau)}\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}0$ (resp. $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(b_i'',1,1-\tau)}\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}0$). Possibly passing to a subsequence, we may assume that $e_i''$ (resp. $b_i''$) is strictly increasing. If $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(1,e_i'',s)}\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}0$ (resp. $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(b_i'',1,s)}\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}0$) for any $s\in [0,1]$ for $i\in\Lambda$ for an infinite set $\Lambda\subset\mathbb N^+$, then we get a contradiction to Lemma~\ref{lem: no part 2 case} as $\{e_i''\}_{i\in\Lambda}$ (resp.  $\{b_i''\}_{i\in\Lambda}$) is not a finite set. Thus possibly passing to a subsequence, we may assume that $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(1,e_i'',s)}\not\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}0$ (resp. $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(b_i'',1,s)}\not\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}0$) for any $s\in [0,1]$ such that $s\neq1-\tau$. By Lemma~\ref{lem: one lc place one close to one}, $e_i''<1-\tau_{\operatorname{aux}}(d,\Gamma\cup\{1-\tau\})$ (resp. $b_i''<1-\tau_{\operatorname{aux}}(d,\Gamma\cup\{1-\tau\})$) for any $i$. This is not possible as $\lim_{i\rightarrow+\infty}e_i''=1$ (resp. $\lim_{i\rightarrow+\infty}b_i''=1$). 

Therefore, possibly passing to a subsequence, we may assume that $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(1,1,1-\tau)}$ is not ample$/T_i$ for any $i$. Since $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(1,1,t_i)}\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}K_{\mathfrak{C}_i''(t_i)}$ is ample$/T_i$, there exists $t_i''\in [1-\tau,t_i)$ such that $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(1,1,t_i'')}\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}0$. By Lemma~\ref{lem: one lc place one close to one}, $t_i''\not\in (1-\tau_{\operatorname{aux}}(d,\Gamma),1)$. Thus
$$1-\tau\leq t_i'\leq 1-\tau_{\operatorname{aux}}(d,\Gamma)<1-\tau,$$
a contradiction.

\medskip

\noindent\textbf{Step 4.} We conclude the proof in this step. 

Suppose that we are in \textbf{Case 2}. Then $t_i=t_i'$ and $$K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(e_i,t_i)}\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_i''(t_i)}\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}0.$$ 
We get a contradiction to \textbf{Step 3} as the coefficients of $B_i''^o+e_iE_i''$ 
belong to the DCC set $\Gamma\cup\{e_i\}_{i=1}^{+\infty}$, $e_i$ is strictly increasing, and $\lim_{i\rightarrow+\infty}e_i=1$. Therefore, we are in \textbf{Case 1}, and $t_i'=1-\tau$ for any $i$. 

Possibly passing to a subsequence, we may assume that $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(1,1-\tau)}$ is ample$/T_i$ for each $i$ or $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(1,1-\tau)}$ is not ample$/T_i$ for each $i$. If $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(1,1-\tau)}$ is ample$/T_i$ for each $i$, then there exists $e_i'\in (e_i,1)$ such that $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(e_i',1-\tau)}\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}0$. Possibly passing to a subsequence, we may assume that $e_i'$ is strictly increasing. Then $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(e_i',1-\tau)}\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}0$. Since the coefficients of $B_i''^o+e_i'E_i''$ and $1-\tau$ belong to the DCC set $\Gamma\cup\{e_i'\}_{i=1}^{+\infty}\cup\{1-\tau\}$, $e_i'$ is strictly increasing and $\lim_{i\rightarrow+\infty}e_i'=1$, we get a contradiction to \textbf{Step 3}. Therefore, $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(1,1-\tau)}$ is not ample$/T_i$ for each $i$. 

Since $t_i>1-\tau$, $\tau<\tau_{\operatorname{ilct}}(d,\Gamma)$, and ${\mathfrak{B}}_i(t_i)$ is lc, ${\mathfrak{B}}_i(1)$ is lc. Let
$$\mathfrak{C}_i':=(X_i',\mathcal{F}_i',B_i'+E_i,{\bf{M}}^i)(1),$$
then $K_{\mathfrak{C}_i'}\geq h^*K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_i(1)}$. Since $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_i(1)}$ is ample$/U_i$, $K_{\mathfrak{C}_i'}$ is big$/U_i$. Thus $\phi_{i,*}K_{\mathfrak{C}_i'}$ is big$/U_i$, hence
$$K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(1,1)}\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}\phi_{i,*}K_{\mathfrak{C}_i'}$$
is ample$/T_i$. Therefore, there exists $t_i''\in [1-\tau,1)$ such that $K_{{\mathfrak{D}}_i(1,t_i'')}\sim_{\mathbb R,T_i}0$. By Lemma~\ref{lem: one lc place one close to one}, $t_i''\not\in (1-\tau_{\operatorname{aux}}(d,\Gamma),1)$, so
$$1-\tau\leq t_i''\leq 1-\tau_{\operatorname{aux}}(d,\Gamma)<1-\tau,$$
a contradiction.

\label{thm: pet general}
    Let $d$ be a positive integer and $\Gamma\subset [0,+\infty)$ a DCC set. Then there exists a positive real number $\tau=\tau_{\operatorname{pet}}(d,\Gamma)$ depending only on $d$ and $\Gamma$ satisfying the following. 

    Let ${\mathfrak{B}}/U$ and ${\mathfrak{B}}'/U$ be two algebraically integrable normalized foliated structures of dimension $d$. Assume that
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item ${\mathfrak{B}}/U\in\Gamma$,
        \item ${\mathfrak{B}}/U\geq{\mathfrak{B}}'/U\geq{\mathfrak{B}}^{1-\tau}/U$,
        \item ${\mathfrak{B}}'$ is lc and $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'}$ is not pseudo-effective$/U$, and
        \item ${\mathfrak{B}}''/U$ is a normalized foliated structure such that $${\mathfrak{B}}^{\epsilon}\cdot{\mathfrak{B}}'^{1-\epsilon}/U\geq{\mathfrak{B}}''/U\geq{\mathfrak{B}}'/U$$
        for some $\epsilon\in (0,1)$.
    \end{enumerate}
    Then $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}''}$ is not pseudo-effective$/U$.

Let $d$ be a positive integer and $\Gamma\subset [0,+\infty)$ a DCC set. Then there exists a positive real number $\tau=\tau_{\operatorname{Rct}}(d,\Gamma)$ depending only on $d$ and $\Gamma$ satisfying the following. 

Assume that ${\mathfrak{B}}/U$ and ${\mathfrak{B}}'/U$ are two algebraically integrable normalized foliated structures of dimension $d$. Assume that
\begin{enumerate}

    \item the parameter $t$ of ${\mathfrak{B}}$ is $<1$.
\end{enumerate}

      of dimension $d$, such that
       \begin{itemize}
       \item $X_i$ is of Fano type over $U_i$,
           \item ${\mathfrak{B}}_i/U_i\in\Gamma$ and $t_i<1$,
           \item        ${\mathfrak{B}}_i/U_i\geq{\mathfrak{B}}_i'/U_i\geq{\mathfrak{B}}_i^{1-\tau_i}/U_i$, 
           \item ${\mathfrak{B}}_i'/U_i$ is $\mathbb R$-complementary, and
           \item ${\mathfrak{B}}_i/U_i$ is not $\mathbb R$-complementary.
       \end{itemize}
       Possibly replacing $X_i$ with a small $\mathbb Q$-factorialization and replacing ${\mathfrak{B}}_i,{\mathfrak{B}}_i'$ with their pullbacks, we may assume that $X_i$ is $\mathbb Q$-factorial for each $i$. We run a $\left(-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_i}\right)$-MMP$/U_i$ with scaling of an ample divisor which terminates with either a good minimal model$/U_i$ $Y_i$, or a Mori fiber space$/U_i$ $f_i: Y_i\rightarrow Z_i$. Let ${\mathfrak{B}}_{Y_i}$ and ${\mathfrak{B}}_{Y_i'}$ be the images of ${\mathfrak{B}}_i,{\mathfrak{B}}_i'$ on $Y_i$ for each $i$. Then ${\mathfrak{B}}_{Y_i}'/U_i$ is $\mathbb R$-complementary. In particular, ${\mathfrak{B}}_{Y_i}'$ is lc. By Theorem~\ref{thm: acc lct general version}, possibly passing to a subsequence, we have that ${\mathfrak{B}}_{Y_i}$ is lc. There are two cases.

       \medskip

       \noindent\textbf{Case 1.} There exists a $(-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_{Y_i}})$-Mori fiber space$/U_i$ $f_i: Y_i\rightarrow Z_i$. Let ${\mathfrak{B}}_{Y_i}(s):={\mathfrak{B}}_{Y_i}^{s}\cdot{\mathfrak{B}}_{Y_i}'^{1-s}$ for any $s\in [0,1]$. Since $-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'_{i}}$ is pseudo-effective$/U_i$, $-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'_{Y_i}}=-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_{Y_i}(0)}$ is pseudo-effective$/U_i$. Since $\rho(Y_i/Z_i)=1$ and $-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_{Y_i}}=-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_{Y_i}(1)}$ is anti-ample$/Z_i$, there exists $\epsilon_i\in [0,1)$ such that $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_{Y_i}(\epsilon_i)}\sim_{\mathbb R,Z_i}0$. Since $\lim_{i\rightarrow+\infty}\tau_i=0$ and
       $${\mathfrak{B}}_{Y_i}(\epsilon_i)/U_i\geq{\mathfrak{B}}_{Y_i}'/U_i\geq{\mathfrak{B}}_{Y_i}^{1-\tau_i}/U_i,$$
       by Proposition~\ref{prop: global acc in bb}, possibly passing to a subsequence, we have that $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_{Y_i}(s)}\sim_{\mathbb R,Z_i}0$ for any $s\in [\epsilon_i,1]$. In particular, $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_{Y_i}}=K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_{Y_i}(1)}\sim_{\mathbb R,Z_i}0$. This is not possible as $f_i$ is a $(-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_{Y_i}})$-Mori fiber space.

       \medskip

       \noindent\textbf{Case 2.} $-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_{Y_i}}$ is semi-ample$/U_i$. In this case, since $t_i<1$, by \cite[Theorem~3.28]{Cas+25a}, we may pick $0\leq D_{Y_i}\sim_{\mathbb R,U_i}-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_{Y_i}}$ such that $({\mathfrak{B}}_{Y_i},D_{Y_i})$ is lc. Let $p_i: W_i\rightarrow X_i$ and $q_i: W_i\rightarrow Y_i$ be a resolution of indeterminacies of the induced birational map $\phi_i: X_i\dashrightarrow Y_i$, and let 
       $$K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_i}+D_i:=p_{i,*}q_i^*(K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_{Y_i}}+D_{Y_i}).$$
       Since $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_{Y_i}}+D_{Y_i}\sim_{\mathbb R,U_i}0$, $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_i}+D_i\sim_{\mathbb R,U_i}0$, and
       $$p_i^*(K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_i}+D_i)=q_i^*(K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_{Y_i}}+D_{Y_i}).$$
       Since $\phi_i$ is $\left(-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_i}\right)$-negative, we have
       $$p_i^*K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_i}\leq q_i^*K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_{Y_i}},$$
       hence
       $$p_i^*D_i\geq q_i^*D_{Y_i}\geq 0.$$
       Therefore, $D_i\geq 0$. Since $({\mathfrak{B}}_{Y_i},D_{Y_i})$ is lc, $({\mathfrak{B}}_i,D_i)$ is lc. Thus $({\mathfrak{B}}_i,D_i)/U_i$ is an $\mathbb R$-complement of ${\mathfrak{B}}_i/U_i$, a contradiction.

Let ${\mathfrak{B}}(s):=(X,\mathcal{F},B,{\bf{M}})(s)$ for any $s\in [0,1]$. We have that 
$$mK_{{\mathfrak{B}}}+L=K_{{\mathfrak{B}}(0)}+(m-1)K_{{\mathfrak{B}}\left(\frac{mt}{m-1}\right)}=K_X+\left(B+{\bf{M}}_X+L+(m-1)K_{{\mathfrak{B}}\left(\frac{mt}{m-1}\right)}\right).$$

$$m-1>\frac{m_0(1-t)}{1-\frac{mt}{m-1}},$$
by Lemma~\ref{lem: potentially birational for afs},
$$D:=B+{\bf{M}}_X+L+(m-1)K_{{\mathfrak{B}}\left(\frac{mt}{m-1}\right)}$$
is potentially birational. Moreover, $D=mK_{{\mathfrak{B}}}+L-K_X$ is an integral divisor. By \cite[Lemma~2.3.4]{HMX13}, 
$$|mK_{{\mathfrak{B}}}+L|=|K_X+\lceil D\rceil|$$
defines a birational map.

We say that ${\mathfrak{B}}$ is a \emph{$(d,r,\Gamma)$-normalized foliated structure} if
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $\dim X=d$, ${\mathfrak{B}}\in\Gamma$, and $t<1$, and
    \item there exists a very ample divisor $A$ on $X$ such that $$A^d\leq r \quad \text{and} \quad A-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}(s)} \text{ is pseudo-effective for any }s\in [0,1].$$
\end{enumerate}
If $\Gamma=\frac{1}{p}\mathbb N$, then we say that ${\mathfrak{B}}$ is a \emph{$(d,r,p)$-normalized foliated structure}. 

We say that ${\mathfrak{B}}$ is a \emph{$(d,r,\Gamma,\epsilon)$} (resp. \emph{$(d,r,p,\epsilon)$})\emph{-normalized foliated structure} if ${\mathfrak{B}}$ is a $(d,r,\Gamma)$ (resp. $(d,r,p)$)-normalized foliated structure and ${\mathfrak{B}}(0)$ is $\epsilon$-klt. We denote by 
$$\mathcal{N}_{d,r,\Gamma}:=\{{\mathfrak{B}}\mid {\mathfrak{B}}\text{ is an algebraically integrable }(d,r,\Gamma)\text{-normalized foliated structure}\},$$
$$\mathcal{N}_{d,r,\Gamma,\epsilon}:=\{{\mathfrak{B}}\mid {\mathfrak{B}}\in\mathcal{N}_{d,r,\Gamma},{\mathfrak{B}}(0)\text{ is }\epsilon\text{-klt}\},\quad \mathcal{N}_{d,r,p}:=\mathcal{N}_{d,r,\frac{1}{p}\mathbb N},\quad \text{and}\quad \mathcal{N}_{d,r,p,\epsilon}:=\mathcal{N}_{d,r,\frac{1}{p}\mathbb N,\epsilon}.$$

    Let $d$ and $p$ be two positive integers, $\epsilon$ a positive real number, and $C$ a positive real number. Then there exists a positive integer $r$ depending only on $d$, $p$, and $C$ satisfying the following. Assume that
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item ${\mathfrak{B}}=(X,\mathcal{F},B,{\bf{M}})(t)$ is a projective klt algebraically integrable normalized foliated structure,
        \item $\dim X=d$, ${\mathfrak{B}}\in\frac{1}{p}\mathbb N$, and $t\in (0,1)$.
        \item $pK_{{\mathfrak{B}}}$ is integral and $|pK_{{\mathfrak{B}}}|$ defines a birational map.
        \item $f: W\rightarrow X$ is a projective birational morphism such that
        $$f^*(pK_{{\mathfrak{B}}})\sim A_W+R_W$$
        where $|A_W|$ is the movable part of $f^*|pK_{{\mathfrak{B}}}|$, $A_W$ is base-point-free and defines a birational morphism $g: W\rightarrow Y$.
        \item ${\mathfrak{B}}_W:=\left(f^{-1}_*{\mathfrak{B}},\left(1-\frac{1}{p}\right)\operatorname{Exc}(f)\right)$ is $\epsilon$-lc.
        \item $\operatorname{vol}(K_{{\mathfrak{B}}})\leq C$.

Then there exists a birational map$/Y$ $\gamma: W\dashrightarrow X'$ which does not extract any divisor satisfying the following. Let ${\mathfrak{B}}':=\gamma_*{\mathfrak{B}}_W$, then $X'$ is $\mathbb Q$-factorial and
$${\mathfrak{B}}'\in \mathcal{N}_{d,r,p,\epsilon}.$$
In particular, ${\mathfrak{B}}'$ belongs to a bounded family, and ${\mathfrak{B}}$ and ${\mathfrak{B}}_W$ belong to a log birationally bounded family.
