Possibly replacing $W$ by a small $\mathbb Q$-factorialization, we may assume that $W$ is $\mathbb Q$-factorial. Let $A_Y:=g_*A_W$. Then $A_Y$ is very ample and $A_Y^d\leq\operatorname{vol}(pK_{{\mathfrak{B}}})\leq p^dC$. Therefore, $Y$ belongs to a bounded family. We may assume that $A_W\geq 0$.

Since ${\mathfrak{B}}_W$ is $\mathbb Q$-factorial klt, by \cite[Theorem~2.1.1]{Cas+25a}, we may run a $(K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_W}+3dA_W)$-MMP with scaling of an ample divisor. By the length of extremal rays, this is also a $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_W}$-MMP$/Y$ with scaling of an ample divisor, which terminates with a good minimal model ${\mathfrak{B}}_Z/Y$ of ${\mathfrak{B}}_W/Y$ associated with a birational map $\phi\colon W\dashrightarrow Z$, where $Z$ is the ambient variety of ${\mathfrak{B}}_Z$. Let $g_Z: Z\rightarrow Y$ be the associated contraction and $A_Z:=\phi_*A_W$. Then $A_Z=g_Z^*A_Y$. 

Let ${\mathfrak{B}}_W(s):=\left(f^{-1}_*{\mathfrak{B}}(s),\left(1-\frac{1}{p}\right)\operatorname{Exc}(f)\right)$
and ${\mathfrak{B}}_Z(s):=\phi_*{\mathfrak{B}}_W(s)$ for any $s\in [0,1]$. Since ${\mathfrak{B}}_W$ is $\epsilon$-lc, ${\mathfrak{B}}_Z$ is $\epsilon$-lc. By \cite[Proposition~9.1]{Cas+25a}, ${\mathfrak{B}}_Z(0)$ is $\epsilon$-lc. By the length of extremal rays, $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_Z(0)}+2dA_Z$ is pseudo-effective. Thus $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_Z(0)}+3dA_Z$ is big.

We run a $(K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_{Z}(0)}+3dA_Z)$-MMP with scaling of an ample divisor. By the length of extremal rays, this MMP is a $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_Z(0)}$-MMP$/Y$ with scaling of an ample divisor and terminates with a good minimal model ${\mathfrak{B}}'(0)/Y$ of ${\mathfrak{B}}_Z(0)/Y$ associated with a birational map $\psi: Z\dashrightarrow X'$ and a contraction $g': X'\rightarrow Y$, where ${\mathfrak{B}}':=\psi_*{\mathfrak{B}}_Z$ and ${\mathfrak{B}}'(s):=\psi_*{\mathfrak{B}}_Z(s)$ for any $s\in [0,1]$. Let $A':=\psi_*A_Z$.

Since ${\mathfrak{B}}_Z(0)$ is $\epsilon$-lc, ${\mathfrak{B}}'(0)$ is $\epsilon$-lc. By Lemma~\ref{lem: volume monotonicity}, we have
\begin{align*}
    0&<\operatorname{vol}(K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'(0)}+3dA')=\operatorname{vol}(K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_Z(0)}+3dA_Z)\leq\left(\frac{1}{1-t}\right)^d\operatorname{vol}(K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_Z}+3dA_Z)\\
    &=\left(\frac{1}{1-t}\right)^d\operatorname{vol}(K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_W}+3dA_W)\leq l^d\operatorname{vol}(K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_W}+3dA_W).
\end{align*}
Since ${\mathfrak{B}}$ is klt and $pK_{{\mathfrak{B}}}$ is integral, we have
$$\left\lfloor pK_{{\mathfrak{B}}_W}\right\rfloor=pf^{-1}_*K_{{\mathfrak{B}}}+p(\operatorname{Exc}(f)^{\operatorname{ninv}}+(1-t)\operatorname{Exc}(f)^{\operatorname{inv}})-\operatorname{Exc}(f)\geq \lfloor f^*(pK_{{\mathfrak{B}}})\rfloor\sim A_W+\lfloor R_W\rfloor,$$
so 
$$\operatorname{vol}(K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_W}+3dA_W)\leq (3dp+1)^d\operatorname{vol}(K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_W})\leq (3dp+1)^d\operatorname{vol}(K_{{\mathfrak{B}}})\leq (3dp+1)^dC.$$
Let $h\colon X'\rightarrow X''$ be the ample model of $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'(0)}+3dA'$. This is also the ample model$/Y$ of $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'(0)}$ by the length of extremal rays. Let $A'':=h_*A'$ and ${\mathfrak{B}}''(s):=h_*{\mathfrak{B}}'(s)$ for any $s\in [0,1]$. Then we have
$$\operatorname{vol}(K_{{\mathfrak{B}}''(0)}+3dA'')=\operatorname{vol}(K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'(0)}+3dA')\in\left(0,(3dp+1)^dC\right).$$
By \cite[Lemma~6.6]{BH22}, $({\mathfrak{B}}''(0),3d\overline{A_Y})$ is bounded. Thus there exists a positive integer $r_1$ depending only on $d$, $p$, and $\epsilon$, and a very ample divisor $H_1$ on $X''$, such that
$$H_1-2(K_{{\mathfrak{B}}''(0)}+3dA'') \text{ is pseudo-effective}, \quad \text{and}\quad H_1^d\leq r_1.$$ We may assume that $H_1$ is general in $|H_1|$. Write
$${\mathfrak{B}}'(s):=(X',\mathcal{F}',B',{\bf{M}})(s)$$
for any $s\in [0,1]$. By \cite[Theorem~2.3]{Bir24}, $(X',B'+h^*H_1)$ belongs to a bounded family. Thus there exists a positive integer $r_2$ and a very ample divisor $H_2$ on $X'$ such that $H_2^d\leq r_2$ and $H_2-h^*H_1$ is pseudo-effective. Therefore,
$$H_2-(K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'(0)}+3dA')=H_2-h^*H_1+h^*(H_1-(K_{{\mathfrak{B}}''(0)}+3dH_2))$$
is pseudo-effective. Therefore, $({\mathfrak{B}}''(0),3d\overline{A_Y})$ is bounded. Since $A_Y$ is very ample, there exists a positive real number $b$ depending only on $d$, $p$, and $\epsilon$, such that
$$bH_2-A'\quad \text{and}\quad bA'-H_2$$
are pseudo-effective. We let $\alpha: V\rightarrow Z$ and $\beta: V\rightarrow X'$ be a resolution of indeterminacies of $\psi$. Then we have
$$\beta_*\alpha^*(K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_Z}+3dA_Z)=K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'}+3dA'.$$
Since $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_Z}+3dA_Z$ and $\beta^*H_2$ are nef, we have
\begin{align*}
    (K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'}+3dA')\cdot H_2^{d-1}=&\alpha^*(K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_{Z}}+3dA_Z)\cdot(\beta^*H_2)^{d-1}\leq\operatorname{vol}(\alpha^*(K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_{Z}}+3dA_Z)+\beta^*H_2)\\
    \leq&\operatorname{vol}(\alpha^*(K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_{Z}}+3dA_Z)+b\beta^*A')=\operatorname{vol}(\alpha^*(K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_{Z}}+(3d+b)A_Z))\\
    =&\operatorname{vol}(K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_{Z}}+(3d+b)A_Z)=\operatorname{vol}(K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_{W}}+(3d+b)A_W)\\
    \leq&(3dq+bp+1)^d\operatorname{vol}(K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_W})\\
    \leq&(3dq+bp+1)^dC=:C_1.
\end{align*}
Since $p^2K_{{\mathfrak{B}}_W}$ is an integral divisor and
$$\left\lfloor pK_{{\mathfrak{B}}_W}\right\rfloor\geq \lfloor f^*(pK_{{\mathfrak{B}}})\rfloor\sim A_W+\lfloor R_W\rfloor\geq 0,$$
we may write
$$pK_{{\mathfrak{B}}_W}\sim L_W\geq 0$$
such that the coefficients of $L_W$ are $\geq\frac{1}{p}$. We let $L':=\psi_*\phi_*L_W$. Then $L'\sim pK_{{\mathfrak{B}}'(t)}$ and $L'\cdot H_2^{d-1}\leq pC_1$. Therefore, $(X',L')$ belongs to a bounded family. Thus there exists a positive integer $c$ depending only on $d$, $p$, and $\epsilon$, such that
$$cH_2-(L'+3dA')$$
is pseudo-effective. Thus 
$$cpH_2-(K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'(t)}+3dA')=cpH_2-t(K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'(1)}+3dA')-(1-t)(K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'(0)}+3dA')$$
is pseudo-effective. Since $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'(0)}+3dA'$ is nef and $t\geq\frac{1}{p}$,
$$cpH_2-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'(1)}$$
is pseudo-effective. Since $H_2-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'(0)}$ is pseudo-effective, 
$$cpH_2-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'(s)}$$
is pseudo-effective for any $s\in [0,1]$. 

Let $r:=(cp)^dr_2$ and $A:=cpH_2$. Then:
\begin{itemize}
    \item $\dim{\mathfrak{B}}'=d,{\mathfrak{B}}'\in\frac{1}{p}\mathbb N$, and $t<1$, and
    \item $A^d\leq r$ and $A-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'(s)}$ is pseudo-effective for any $s\in [0,1]$.
    \item ${\mathfrak{B}}'(0)$ is $\epsilon$-lc.
\end{itemize}
Therefore, 
$${\mathfrak{B}}'\in\mathcal{N}_{d,r,p,\epsilon}.$$
By Lemma~\ref{lem: drii0 is bounded}, ${\mathfrak{B}}'$ belongs to a bounded family.
Let $\gamma:=\psi\circ\phi$ be the induced birational map. Then $\gamma$ does not extract any divisor, hence ${\mathfrak{B}}_W$ is log birationally bounded. By our definition of ${\mathfrak{B}}_W$, we have that $\operatorname{Supp} B'$ contains all $f$-exceptional prime divisors. Thus ${\mathfrak{B}}$ is log birationally bounded.

By Theorem~, there exists a positive integer q depending only on d and p such that pmid q, qK_B is an integral divisor, and |qK_B| defines a birational map. We let phi_X: Xdashrightarrow mathbb P^n_X be the birational map induced by |qK_B| and let Y be the normalization of the closure of phi_X(X). Let phicolon Xdashrightarrow Y be the induced birational map. We let f': W'rightarrow X and g': W'rightarrow Y be a resolution of indeterminacies of phi such that f' is a log resolution of B. We let B_W':=left(f'^-1_*B,left(1-frac1qright)Exc(f')right). Since B is klt, B_W' is klt. We let S:=left\Emiddle| E is exceptional/W', a(E,B_W')leq left(-1+frac1qright)(tepsilon_F(E)+(1-t))right\, then S is a finite set by . By , there exists a projective birational morphism pi: Wrightarrow W' such that Exc(pi) contains exactly all prime divisors that are contained in S. Let B_W:=left(pi^-1_*B_W',left(1-frac1qright)Exc(pi)right). Then B_W is frac1pq-lc. Let f:=f'circpi and g:=g'circpi. By the construction of phi, we have that f^*(qK_B)sim A_W+R_W such that A_W is base-point-free, |A_W| is the movable part of |f^*(qK_B)|=f^*|qK_B|, and defines g: Wrightarrow Y. The lemma follows.

Let $\phi\colon X\dashrightarrow Y$ be the induced birational map. 

We let $f': W'\rightarrow X$ and $g': W'\rightarrow Y$ be a resolution of indeterminacies of $\phi$ such that $f'$ is a log resolution of ${\mathfrak{B}}$. We let
$${\mathfrak{B}}_{W'}:=\left(f'^{-1}_*{\mathfrak{B}},\left(1-\frac{1}{q}\right)\operatorname{Exc}(f')\right).$$
Since ${\mathfrak{B}}$ is klt, ${\mathfrak{B}}_{W'}$ is klt. We let 
$$\mathcal{S}:=\left\{E\middle| E\text{ is exceptional}/W', a(E,{\mathfrak{B}}_{W'})\leq \left(-1+\frac{1}{q}\right)(t\epsilon_{\mathcal{F}}(E)+(1-t))\right\},$$

Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the foliation induced by $f$. 

We first show that $f$ is lc. We let $h_T: T'\rightarrow T$ be a resolution of $T$ and let $f': X'\rightarrow T'$ be the base change of $f$. Then $f': X'\rightarrow T'$ is BP stable (cf.~\cite[Definition~2.5]{ACSS21}). To see this, simply note that for any resolution $g_{T'}: T''\rightarrow T'$ and base change $f'': X''\rightarrow T''$ associated with $g: X''\rightarrow X'$ we have that $K_{X''/T''}=g^*K_{X'/T'}$. We can also simply take $T'$ to be a sufficiently high resolution and \cite[Theorem~1]{Sho23} applies.

Now let $\mathcal{F}'$ be the foliation induced by $f'$ and let $h: X'\rightarrow X$ be the associated birational morphism. Since $f$ is stable, 
$$h^*K_{X/T}=K_{X'/T'}=K_{\mathcal{F}'},$$
hence
$$K_{\mathcal{F}}=h_*K_{X'/T'}=K_{X/T}\quad \text{and}\quad h^*K_{\mathcal{F}}=K_{\mathcal{F}'}.$$
We have that $\mathcal{F}'$ satisfies Property $(*)$ and $f'$ is equidimensional, so by \cite[Proposition~3.7]{ACSS21}, $\mathcal{F}'$ is lc. By \cite[Proposition~2.15]{PX17}, $K_{\mathcal{F}'}$ is big and nef.

Since $K_{X'/T'}$ is $\mathbb Q$-Cartier and $f'^*K_{T'}$ is Cartier, it follows that $K_{X'}$ is $\mathbb Q$-Cartier. Since $\mathcal{F}'$ satisfies Property $(*)$, $X'$ is lc. By Theorem~\ref{thm: big gap general}, there exists a real number $t$ depending only on $d$ such that $K_{t}':=tK_{\mathcal{F}'}+(1-t)K_{X'}$ is big. Thus $K_t:=h_*K_t'$ is big. This implies (1). Since $h$ does not extract any divisor, under the conditions of (2),
$$0<\operatorname{vol}(K_t')\leq\operatorname{vol}(K_t)\leq C.$$
By Theorem~\ref{thm: birationally bounded main}, $(X',\mathcal{F}')$ is log birationally bounded. Thus $(X,\mathcal{F})$ is log birationally bounded, which implies (2).

Let $\tau:=\tau_{\operatorname{Rct}}(d,\Gamma\cup\{1\})$ as in Theorem~\ref{thm: rct general}. We let $t':=\min\{t,1-\tau\}$. By Lemma~\ref{lem: gap exc threshold}, ${\mathfrak{B}}'(t')$ is exceptional.

Pick any $0\leq D'\sim_{\mathbb R}-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'(t')}$ and let $\mathfrak{C}':=({\mathfrak{B}}'(t'),D')$. Then $\mathfrak{C}'$ is klt and $K_{\mathfrak{C}'}\sim_{\mathbb R}0$. Let $\mathfrak{C}:=h_*\mathfrak{C}'$, then $K_{\mathfrak{C}}\sim_{\mathbb R}0$ and $\mathfrak{C}'=h^*\mathfrak{C}$. If $\mathfrak{C}$ is $\tau$-lc, then by \cite[Theorem~2.4.1]{Cas+25a}, $(X,\mathcal{F})$ belongs to a bounded family. In particular, $X$ belongs to a bounded family, so there exists a positive integer $r$ depending only on $d$ and $\Gamma$, and a very ample divisor $H$ on $X$, such that $H^d\leq r$ and $-r\leq K_X\cdot H^{d-1}$. Let $\mathfrak{C}'(s):=({\mathfrak{B}}'(s),D')$ for any $s\in [0,1]$. Since $K_{\mathfrak{C}'}\sim_{\mathbb R}0$ and $\mathfrak{C}'$ is klt, by \cite[Theorem~5.1]{Cas+25a}, $K_{\mathfrak{C}'(1)}$ is pseudo-effective, hence $-K_{\mathfrak{C}'(0)}$ is pseudo-effective. Thus
$$-K_{\mathfrak{C}'(0)}\cdot(h^*H)^{d-1}\geq 0.$$
Therefore,
$$-r\leq K_X\cdot H^{d-1}\leq (K_X+B+{\bf{M}}_X)\cdot H^{d-1}\leq 0.$$
Since ${\mathfrak{B}}\in\Gamma$, possibly replacing $r$ by a multiple depending only on $\Gamma$, we have that
$$-r\leq K_X\cdot H^{d-1}\leq (K_X+\operatorname{Supp} B+{\bf{M}}_X)\cdot H^{d-1}\leq 0.$$
Thus ${\mathfrak{B}}$ belongs to a bounded family.

Therefore, we may assume that $\mathfrak{C}$ is not $\tau$-lc, so $\mathfrak{C}'$ is not $\tau$-lc. Let $E$ be a prime divisor over $X'$ such that $a(E,\mathfrak{C}')={\operatorname{tmld}}(\mathfrak{C}')$. Since $1-t'\geq\tau$, $a(E,\mathfrak{C}')<0$. If $E$ is on $X'$, then we let $g: X'\rightarrow X'$ be the identity morphism and let
$${\mathfrak{B}}'':=(X',\mathcal{F}',B'+(\operatorname{mult}_ED')E,{\bf{M}})(t'),$$
and if $E$ is not on $X$, then since $t'<1$, by \cite[Theorem~2.2.3]{Cas+25a}, there exists a projective birational morphism $g: Y\rightarrow X'$ which extracts exactly $E$, and we let $${\mathfrak{B}}'':=(g^{-1}_*{\mathfrak{B}}'(t'),E).$$
Moreover, $Y$ is of Fano type. 

In either case, by Theorem~\ref{thm: rct general}, ${\mathfrak{B}}''$ is $\mathbb R$-complementary. Let $({\mathfrak{B}}'',L)$ be an $\mathbb R$-complement of ${\mathfrak{B}}''$, then $(g_*{\mathfrak{B}}'',g_*L)$ is an $\mathbb R$-complement of $g_*{\mathfrak{B}}''$ that is not klt, and hence an $\mathbb R$-complement of ${\mathfrak{B}}'(t')$ that is not klt. Therefore, ${\mathfrak{B}}'(t')$ is not exceptional, a contradiction.

$$D':=\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^l\frac{r_i}{l}D_{i,j}.$$
Then for any closed point $x\in X$, there exists a finite set $\Lambda=\Lambda(x)$ such that $\#\Lambda\leq d$ and $x\in\operatorname{Supp} D_{i,j}$ if and only if $(i,j)\in\Lambda$. Since $l\gg 0$ and $L$ is big, we have that
$$\epsilon L-\frac{d}{l}\sum_{i=1}^mD_i$$
is big, hence
$$\epsilon L-\sum_{(i,j)\in\Lambda(x)}\frac{r_i}{l}D_{i,j}$$
is big for any closed point $x\in X$. Thus we may pick
$$D_x:=\sum_{(i,j)\in\Lambda(x)}\frac{r_i}{l}D_{i,j}\leq H_x\sim_{\mathbb R}\epsilon L,$$
and we have
\begin{align*}

\end{align*}
Thus
$$\alpha(X,B+D';L)=\inf_{x\in X}\alpha(X\ni x,B+D';L)\geq\alpha(X,B;L)-\epsilon$$
and the lemma follows.

We may assume that $\dim X\geq 2$, otherwise $X=\mathbb P^1$ and $\mathcal{F}=0$ or $T_X$ and there is nothing left to prove.

If $\mathcal{F}=T_X$ or $t=0$, the rational coefficient case was proven in \cite[Corollary~6.14]{LLX20}. The proof of the real coefficient case is similar: By \cite[Lemma~2.13]{XZ24} and \cite[Corollary~1.4]{XZ21}, there exists a positive real number $\epsilon_1$ such that $\widehat{\operatorname{vol}}(X\ni x,B)\geq\epsilon_1$ for any closed point $x\in X$. Here $\widehat{\operatorname{vol}}(X\ni x,B)$ is the local volume (normalized volume) of $(X,B)$ at $x$ (cf.~\cite{Li18,LLX20}). By \cite[Theorem~6.13]{LLX20}, $(X,B)$ is $\frac{\epsilon_1}{d^d}$-lc, and we are done by \cite[Theorem~1.1]{Bir21a}. In the following, we may assume that $\mathcal{F}\neq T_X$ and $t>0$. By (3), $-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}}$ is big and nef. Since $\alpha({\mathfrak{B}})>0$, ${\mathfrak{B}}$ is klt. Thus $t<1$.

We let ${\mathfrak{B}}(s):=(X,\mathcal{F},B)(s)$ for any $s\in [0,1]$.

If ${\mathfrak{B}}$ is canonical, then ${\mathfrak{B}}$ is $\epsilon$-lc. By \cite[Theorem~9.2]{Cas+25a} and \cite[Corollary~1.4]{Bir21a}, $X$ belongs to a bounded family, and if $t\geq\epsilon$, then by \cite[Theorem~2.4.1]{Cas+25a}, $(X,\mathcal{F})$ belongs to a bounded family, so the theorem follows. Therefore, we may assume that ${\mathfrak{B}}$ is not canonical. We let $E$ be a prime divisor over $X$ such that
$$a(E,{\mathfrak{B}})+t\epsilon_{\mathcal{F}}(E)+(1-t)={\operatorname{tmld}}({\mathfrak{B}}).$$
Then $a(E,{\mathfrak{B}})\leq 0$. By \cite[Theorem~1.10(1)]{Cas+24}, $X$ is potentially klt. By \cite[Theorem~2.2.3]{Cas+25a}, we may let $h\colon X'\rightarrow X$ be a small $\mathbb Q$-factorialization of $X$ if $E$ is on $X$, and a birational morphism such that $\operatorname{Exc}(h)=E$ and $X'$ is $\mathbb Q$-factorial if $E$ is not on $X$. We let
$${\mathfrak{B}}'(t):=h^*{\mathfrak{B}}(t):=(X',\mathcal{F}',B')(t)$$
and let 
$${\mathfrak{B}}'(s):=(X',\mathcal{F}',B')(s)$$
for any $s\in [0,1]$. Since ${\mathfrak{B}}$ is klt, ${\mathfrak{B}}'(t)$ is klt. Since $t<1$, by Lemma~\ref{lem: lc preserved under inequality}, ${\mathfrak{B}}'(s)$ is klt for any $s\in [0,t]$. Since $-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}(t)}$ is big, $-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'(t)}$ is big, so $-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'(t-\delta)}$ is big for any $0\leq\delta\ll 1$. By \cite[Theorem~9.2]{Cas+25a}, $X$ and $X'$ are of Fano type. In particular, $-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'(t)}$ is semi-ample. 

By the length of extremal rays \cite[Theorem~1.3(2)]{Cas+24} and the contraction theorem \cite[Theorem~2.1.3]{Cas+25a}, we may pick an integer $n\gg 0$ such that ${\mathfrak{B}}(t-1/n)$ is klt, $-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'(t-1/n)}$ is big, and we may run a $\left(-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'(t-1/n)}\right)$-MMP which terminates with a good minimal model and the MMP is $\left(-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'(t)}\right)$-trivial. We let $\phi\colon X'\dashrightarrow X''$ be this MMP and let ${\mathfrak{B}}''(s):=\phi_*{\mathfrak{B}}'(s):=(X'',\mathcal{F}'',B'')(s)$ for any $s\in [0,1]$. Note that $\phi$ is also a sequence of steps of a $(-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'(0)})$-MMP. Since $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'(0)}=K_{X'}+B'$, $\phi$ is also a sequence of steps of a $\left(-(K_{X'}+B')\right)$-MMP. By our construction, $-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'(t-1/n)}$ and $-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'(t)}$ are big and semi-ample, and
$$K_{X''}+B''+tn\left(-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}''(t-1/n)}\right)=K_{{\mathfrak{B}}''(0)}+tn\left(-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}''(t-1/n)}\right)=(tn-1)(-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}''(t)}).$$
Since $\phi$ and $h$ are $K_{{\mathfrak{B}}'(t)}$-trivial, ${\mathfrak{B}}''(t)$ and ${\mathfrak{B}}(t)$ are crepant, $\alpha({\mathfrak{B}}''(t))=\alpha({\mathfrak{B}})$, and $\operatorname{vol}(-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}''(t)})=\operatorname{vol}(-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}})$. In particular, ${\mathfrak{B}}''(t)$ is klt, so by Lemma~\ref{lem: lc preserved under inequality}, ${\mathfrak{B}}''(s)$ is klt for any $s\in [0,t]$. In particular, ${\mathfrak{B}}''(0)$ is klt, so $(X'',B'')$ is klt. 

Pick any $s>\alpha(X'',B'';-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}''(t)})$. Then we may pick $L_s\in |-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}''(t)}|_{\mathbb R}$ such that $(X'',B''+sL_s)$ is not lc. In particular,
$$\left(X'',B''+s\left(L_s^{\operatorname{ninv}}+\frac{1}{1-t}L_s^{\operatorname{inv}}\right)\right)$$
is not lc. By Lemma~\ref{lem: lc preserved under inequality}, 
$$\left(X'',\mathcal{F}'',B''+s\left(L_s^{\operatorname{ninv}}+\frac{1}{1-t}L_s^{\operatorname{inv}}\right)\right)(t)$$
is not lc, hence $\alpha(X'',B'';-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}''(t)})<s$. Therefore, 
$$\alpha(X'',B'';-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}''(t)})\geq\alpha({\mathfrak{B}}''(t))=\alpha({\mathfrak{B}}).$$
By Lemma~\ref{lem: alpha bound} we may choose $0\leq D\sim_{\mathbb R}-tnK_{{\mathfrak{B}}''(t-1/n)}$ such that 
$$\alpha(X'',B''+D;-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}''(t)})\geq\frac{1}{2}\alpha({\mathfrak{B}}).$$ 
Since
$$K_{X''}+B''+D\sim_{\mathbb R}(tn-1)(-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}''(t)}),$$
we have
$$\alpha(X'',B''+D;K_{X''}+B''+D)=\frac{1}{tn-1}\alpha(X'',B''+D;-K_{{\mathfrak{B}}''(t)})>\frac{1}{2(tn-1)}\alpha({\mathfrak{B}}).$$
Moreover, we have

nodes.name: Non-algebraically integrable case
nodes.statement: As in , we expect that our main theorems remain valid for foliations that are not necessarily algebraically integrable. There are, however, several obstacles to such an extension. The first major obstacle, and the best-known one, is the existence of foliated log resolutions, which is known in dimension leq 3 but remains widely open in dimension geq 4, despite recent progress (cf.). For algebraically integrable foliations, the foliated log resolution we use is essentially the toroidal reduction arising as a step in the weak semi-stable reduction . Nevertheless, we expect that a suitable form of foliated log resolution should exist for arbitrary foliations. A second obstacle, which appears to be more serious, is the failure of the adjunction formula. Although there is a satisfactory adjunction formula for foliations along non-invariant divisors , such a formula fails in general for adjunction along invariant divisors (cf.). For foliated triples, this failure already causes substantial difficulties and requires delicate arguments to obtain a workable adjunction formula, even in dimension 3 (cf., , , ). In fact, the failure of adjunction is the main obstacle in the proofs of the ACC and the global ACC for foliated triples in dimension leq 3 (cf.). For adjoint foliated structures, the failure of adjunction is likely to create further difficulties, since the geometry of singularities is harder to control, especially when the parameter t is very close to 0.

As in \cite{Cas+25a}, we expect that our main theorems remain valid for foliations that are not necessarily algebraically integrable. 

There are, however, several obstacles to such an extension. The first major obstacle, and the best-known one, is the existence of foliated log resolutions, which is known in dimension $\leq 3$ \cite{Sei68,Can04,MP13} but remains widely open in dimension $\geq 4$, despite recent progress (cf.~\cite{AdSTW25}). For algebraically integrable foliations, the foliated log resolution we use is essentially the toroidal reduction \cite[Proposition~4.4]{AK00} arising as a step in the weak semi-stable reduction \cite[Theorem~2.1]{AK00}. Nevertheless, we expect that a suitable form of foliated log resolution should exist for arbitrary foliations.

A second obstacle, which appears to be more serious, is the failure of the adjunction formula. Although there is a satisfactory adjunction formula for foliations along non-invariant divisors \cite[Theorem~1.1]{CS25a}, such a formula fails in general for adjunction along invariant divisors (cf.~\cite[Example~3.20]{CS25a}). For foliated triples, this failure already causes substantial difficulties and requires delicate arguments to obtain a workable adjunction formula, even in dimension $3$ (cf.~\cite[Sections~3 and~4]{Spi20}, \cite[Section~3]{CS21}, \cite[Section~3]{SS22}, \cite[Section~4]{CS25b}). In fact, the failure of adjunction is the main obstacle in the proofs of the ACC and the global ACC for foliated triples in dimension $\leq 3$ (cf.~\cite{Che22,LLM23,LMX24a,LMX24b}). For adjoint foliated structures, the failure of adjunction is likely to create further difficulties, since the geometry of singularities is harder to control, especially when the parameter $t$ is very close to $0$.

In fact, the failure of adjunction is the main obstacle in the proofs of the ACC and the global ACC for foliated triples in dimension leq 3 (cf.). For adjoint foliated structures, the failure of adjunction is likely to create further difficulties, since the geometry of singularities is harder to control, especially when the parameter t is very close to 0.

In another talk of M\textsuperscript{c}Kernan \cite[50:55]{McK23}, the following question is raised: can one obtain an ACC statement for interpolated thresholds between two foliations, instead of between one foliation and $X$? More precisely, consider
    $$\operatorname{lct}(\mathcal{F};\mathcal{G}):=\sup\{t\in [0,1]\mid (\mathcal{G},\mathcal{F},t)\text{ is lc}\},$$
    where $(\mathcal{G},\mathcal{F},t)$ is associated with the canonical class $tK_{\mathcal{G}}+(1-t)K_{\mathcal{F}}$, and ask whether $\operatorname{lct}(\mathcal{F};\mathcal{G})$ belongs to an ACC set whenever $\mathcal{G}\subset\mathcal{F}$. Note that when $\mathcal{F}=T_X$ this is exactly Conjecture~\ref{conj: acc interpolated}. We expect this question to be approachable at least when $\mathcal{F}$ and $\mathcal{G}$ are algebraically integrable. To address it, however, one first needs an existence result for the minimal model program for $(\mathcal{G},\mathcal{F},t)$, which is still open; see \cite[Conjecture~A.10]{Cas+24} for a precise formulation.

    We sketch a possible framework. Consider a structure
    $${\mathfrak{A}}:=(\mathcal{F}_1\subset\mathcal{F}_2\subset\cdots\subset\mathcal{F}_r,(a_1,\dots,a_r)),$$
    where each $\mathcal{F}_i$ is an (algebraically integrable) foliation, $a_i\in (0,1)$, and $\sum_{i=1}^r a_i=1$, and associate to it the canonical class
    $$K_{{\mathfrak{A}}}:=\sum_{i=1}^r a_iK_{\mathcal{F}_i}.$$
    We call ${\mathfrak{A}}$ a \emph{foliated flag} (or, by abuse of terminology, still an adjoint foliated structure). When the ambient variety $X$ is $\mathbb Q$-factorial klt and all $\mathcal{F}_i$ are algebraically integrable, the existence of a minimal model for such a structure is known in the following cases:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item $r=1$ and $\mathcal{F}_r=T_X$, by \cite{BCHM10}, since a foliated flag is then a klt pair.
        \item $r=1$ and $\mathcal{F}_r\neq T_X$, by \cite{ACSS21,CHLX23,CS25c,LMX25}, where a foliated flag is an algebraically integrable foliation.
        \item $r=2$ and $\mathcal{F}_r=T_X$, by \cite{Cas+25a}, where a foliated flag is an algebraically integrable adjoint foliated structure.
    \end{itemize}
    It is then natural to expect the following pattern for the existence of the minimal model program for algebraically integrable foliated flags:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item The case $r=r_0$ and $\mathcal{F}_r=T_X$ implies the case $r=r_0$ and $\mathcal{F}_r\neq T_X$.
        \item The case $r=r_0$ and $\mathcal{F}_r\neq T_X$ implies the case $r=r_0+1$ and $\mathcal{F}_r=T_X$.
    \end{itemize}
    Since we always have $r\leq \dim X+1$, this would yield the existence of the minimal model program for any such ${\mathfrak{A}}$ by induction on $r$.
